Tech Report: Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

📅 12 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4618 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.
  • Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.
  • Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Sources indicate that hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”.

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

Sources indicate that “But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

Sources indicate that “It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”.

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso mentioned: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very notable part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a big topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”.

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

This is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the matter yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury promptly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

Sources indicate that none of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also showed quality and a threat. The joke is right now on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

It is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a upcoming reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

“Before the season, I mentioned to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

In a recent development, “Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”.

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he remarked. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”.

Industry observers note that hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

It has been revealed that belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

Industry observers note that it was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

We had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

Sources indicate that we can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

It has been revealed that there have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

Fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

According to recent reports, and as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”.

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

According to recent reports, alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

In a recent development, you might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

According to recent reports, liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

Hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

Recent findings suggest that that had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

Martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

This game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Recent findings suggest that just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

Bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

Matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well.

Within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

Sources indicate that andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a fresh left-back in due course.

So at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

Recent findings suggest that palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

According to recent reports, one way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

That’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

It has been revealed that this is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

According to recent reports, that’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

It has been revealed that there is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

5 - Morgan Rogers is the fifth different player to score or assist in each of Chelsea's first four games of a Premier League season, after Didier Drogba (2010-11), Cesc Fàbregas (2014-15), Diego Costa (2014-15 & 2016-17), and Eden Hazard (2018-19).Famous. pic.twitter.com/0cuThzH472.

A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

Recent findings suggest that austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

In a recent development, an almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

It has been revealed that wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Sources indicate that morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez launched the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

We’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

Although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

Twelve seconds in and the chant “where were you in Istanbul” gets a very early airing from Villa’s home fans.

That is of course a reference to Villa’s 4-0 win over Forest in the Europa League semi-final second leg last season.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

Xabi Alonso has made an encouraging start to life as Chelsea manager. But his trousers upset me. They are three inches too short and a bit baggy above the ankle.

It has been revealed that we are under way in the five Premier League 3pm kick-offs. Goals and further updates from around the grounds as they happen.

Some early #analysis from Matt at the Bridge, about one of Hull’s midfielders.

Matt Crooks is absolutely massive.

One player who has really shone for Villa so far this season is teenage midfielder George Hemmings.

Unai Emery has been very impressed with the academy graduate, who made his Champions League debut on Tuesday night.

There is also a big buzz around £51m signing Johan Manzambi, who is on the bench today after recovering from a knee injury.

Will we get another fast start from Chelsea today? They have scored inside the first five minutes in all three of their League games this season. Hull are yet to concede.

Dominic King writes that there were signs of promise in the relationship between Barcola, Wirtz and Isak in Liverpool’s win over Atletico Madrid, and all three forwards start against Fulham. Timothy Castagne, Fulham’s right-back will need to have his sprinting boots on against Barcola, who is grease lightning.

Cole Palmer has 15 goal involvements in his 15 Premier League games for Chelsea against newly promoted sides.9 goals ⚽6 assists 🅰️ pic.twitter.com/PJIU0YxIhQ.

It has been revealed that I’m having real fun. I’ve got a smile on face and I’m enjoying my football. Playing with players like [Palmer and Joao Pedro] inspire you to be better and make you do better and do well for the team. We are in a good moment and we want to keep it going.

In a recent development, hull are really tough to beat. They have played against some good opponents and they’ve kept them out - they haven’t conceded yet. It is going to be difficult because they are really organised but we are at home and it is on us to make the game about us.

We know it is always tough against Brentford. We can expect a tight game today, definitely. We both want to win so it’ll be a nice game.

According to recent reports, we are very excited about our first European game coming up but we haven’t really spoken about it lately because we have just spoken about this game. This is a significant game and we are looking for our first three points of the season. We have been close in every game so we hope to get it today.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a newly introduced chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

Recent findings suggest that there have been signs of progress at both of the former European Cup winners. Villa secured an impressive victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday. Forest are improving under Glasner, with their best performance the 2-2 draw at Liverpool.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.

Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez departed for pastures fresh in the transfer window.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this afternoon’s Premier League three o’clock kick-offs, and home bankers would appear to be the theme of the day.

Liverpool will be strongly fancied to put Fulham to the sword at Anfield, with confidence low at the London club and new manager Alvaro Arbeloa (once a player at Anfield) already under pressure amid reports of dressing room unrest. Andoni Iraola secured his first Premier League victory as Liverpool manager at Ipswich last time out, and backed up that result with a come-from-behind win against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

According to recent reports, chelsea host Hull City, who are unbeaten after three games and have yet to concede a goal. It is a remarkable start to the season for Sergej Jakirović‘s side, who continue to defy expectations as well as the underlying data. For all their spirit and defensive organisation, keeping out Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro at Stamford Bridge promises to be a tall order, though.

Aston Villa’s rocky start to the campaign took a turn for the better with a 3-2 Champions League victory at Club Brugge, and as the weeks go by Unai Emery’s team should grow stronger as their raft of young signings bed in. Nottingham Forest could be obdurate opponents, although Villa swept them aside in the second leg of last season’s Europa League semi-final. Oliver Glasner’s Crystal Palace were a bogey team for Villa though, with the Austrian coach undefeated against Emery having notched up some resounding victories.

Industry observers note that glasner’s former club Palace could do with a home win against Ipswich Town, while there is cigarette paper between Bournemouth and Brentford, two of the league’s smartest operators who play at the Vitality Stadium this afternoon. Bournemouth qualified for Europe at Brentford’s expense last season, but Marco Rose is looking for his first league win despite some encouraging performances.

No advantage played and an indirect free-kick: Pairetto criticised for Milan-Frosinone officiating

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Referee Luca Pairetto has been criticised for his performance in AC Milan’s 5-1 win over Frosinone last night.
  • This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) comments on three incidents above all in which the referee ultimately seemed incapable of providing the right decision, one of which could have cost a goal.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Referee Luca Pairetto has been criticised for his performance in AC Milan’s 5-1 win over Frosinone last night.

This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) comments on three incidents above all in which the referee ultimately seemed incapable of providing the right decision, one of which could have cost a goal.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that in the first half, Adrien Rabiot stole the ball from Cittadini, who blatantly dragged him back by the shirt. The ball rolled to Goncalo Ramos who was through on goal and had a man to his left, effectively making it a two-on-zero break with just the goalkeeper to beat.

In a recent development, yet, the referee Pairetto blew his whistle for a foul and demonstrated a yellow card to the defender. He immediately apologised for his error in failing to play the clear advantage for the Rossoneri, in an incident reminiscent of the Junior Messias goal not given against Spezia in 2021-22.

That wasn’t all, either. Nine minutes into the second half, an indirect free-kick was awarded inside the Frosinone penalty area following a clear back-pass from Calvani to Palmisani, that was actually flagged by the assistant referee and not initially given by Pairetto.

Former referee Mauro Bergonzi commented on the refereeing incidents in Milan-Frosinone to La Domenica Sportiva.

“In the first half, the referee failed to take the lead: he missed the lead, he squandered it, if we’re being honest. The situation is this: Cittadini fouls Rabiot, who steals the ball, a clear hold, the referee hastily calls the foul, and he also realises it immediately because he stops, as if to say, ‘Wow, it’s a shame I called’ because Gonçalo Ramos was hurtling toward goal.

Recent findings suggest that “He apologizes, he notes: ‘No, I apologise, I’m booking the Frosinone player.’ He stated sorry. But this is something that really bothers you from a refereeing perspective because the lead was clear, but the referee’s gesture is commendable because he raises his hands and humbly says: ‘I made a mistake’.

“53rd minute: we rarely see them called on football pitches during matches. It’s a deliberate back pass from Calvani to the goalkeeper, the goalkeeper saves it, the referee wouldn’t have called anything, he turns to the right, looks at the assistant because the assistant signals it to him.

“Pairetto tells the assistant, ‘Well done’ and, to make matters worse, ‘Well done’ again. The assistant was good because he saw it perfectly correctly. He made his choice, he got it right because this is a pass, a deliberate back pass.

“Chiffi, the fourth official, is also there, pressing the button to communicate with the refereeing team via his headset, and if the assistant hadn’t seen it, the fourth official would have signaled it.”.

26-year-old steps up to prove his value in absence of influential Blackburn Rovers man: Opinion

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Blackburn Rovers have maintained solid form since the international break, drawing with Burnley before a midweek win over Watford.
  • Injury to Sam Morsy also presented a dilemma for Rovers.
  • However, on hand to step up and soften the blow of Morsy’s absence has been Moussa Baradji.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blackburn Rovers have maintained solid form since the international break, drawing with Burnley before a midweek win over Watford. They’ve had to deal with adversity ahead of those matches too, notably seeing head coach Tony Mowbray step back from his duties for health reasons.

Injury to Sam Morsy also presented a dilemma for Rovers. Since moving to Ewood Park in the summer, the 35-year-old has emerged as a leader and formed a fine partnership with Kristi Montgomery in the middle of the park.

However, on hand to step up and soften the blow of Morsy’s absence has been Moussa Baradji. After some challenging moments in his debut campaign, the 26-year-old midfielder has delivered when needed and proven his value in the Rovers squad.

Sources indicate that baradji joined Blackburn Rovers on an initial loan last summer, and he had to deal with injury in his first season. His impact was limited as a result, and when he was available, fans weren’t too sold on his performances.

In a recent development, despite this, the Frenchman was signed permanently in the summer. When injury hit and Baradji missed the first six games of the latest Championship season, many of the Rovers faithful feared a similar campaign would pan out.

However, Baradji has now played in all of the last 10 Championship games – four have come from the start, two when covering for Montgomery during his injury absence, and two while Morsy has been out. The last two appearances have been the best of the lot, battling hard to help Rovers to a point against Burnley before another well-rounded display in the mature midweek win over Watford.

In a recent development, baradji has brought power in and out of possession in Morsy’s absence. He isn’t afraid to get stuck in and use his stature to muscle opponents off the ball, and his physical attributes, paired with slick footwork, make him a good ball carrier as well.

The midfielder’s per 90 stats highlight the impression he has made when called upon. As per FotMob‘s dataset, Baradji is averaging 1.30 successful dribbles per 90 (top 9% of Championship midfielders), 9.88 duels won (top 1%), 7.64 defensive contributions (top 8%) and a 75% long-ball accuracy rate (top 4%).

Industry observers note that baradji’s signing came with some reservations, as a deal was initially shelved when his medical raised an injury problem. However, the numbers he posted in a competitive Swiss Super League for a relegated Yverdon Sport side revealed exactly why Blackburn Rovers were interested.

It has been revealed that and, his recent performances have started to show that he can be a hit in the Championship too. Baradji pairs power and skill to offer a real force in possession, and his work rate and physicality have seen him offer the strong presence needed in the middle in Morsy’s absence.

Sources indicate that morsy will be backed to reclaim his place when fit. But, at 35, he isn’t a long-term option. Baradji has shown he is ready to stake a claim for a long-term spot in the Rovers team.

Ramos upset by substitution: The clarification and why Cisse came on over Camarda

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (406 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Goncalo Ramos got his name on the scoresheet in AC Milan’s rout of Frosinone, but he was forced off in the second half.
  • Industry observers note that as Sky (via Calciomercato.com) report, everything seemed great when Milan were dominating Frosinone at San Siro and scoring nearly every time they went forward.
  • It has been revealed that ruben Amorim was forced to replace his Ramos in the 50th minute.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Goncalo Ramos got his name on the scoresheet in AC Milan’s rout of Frosinone, but he was forced off in the second half.

Industry observers note that as Sky (via Calciomercato.com) report, everything seemed great when Milan were dominating Frosinone at San Siro and scoring nearly every time they went forward. However, during the second half, a minor alarm sounded.

It has been revealed that ruben Amorim was forced to replace his Ramos in the 50th minute. The Portuguese striker – who had scored in the first half – was hastily removed from the pitch by the head coach shortly after Ardon Jashari’s goal to make it 3-1.

Sources indicate that the reason? The change was made due to a minor muscle problem that the player reported to the bench, even though Ramos himself did not seem happy about the substitution at the time of the change.

It has been revealed that the former PSG man informed the bench that he had a small calf problem and – to avoid worsening the glitch – Amorim immediately opted for a substitution. Alphadjo Cisse was sent on in his place, and he scored the fourth goal just a few minutes later.

When he was taken off, Ramos showed a grimace of disapproval towards his bench, miming the ‘wait’ gesture. He then complained that he would have liked to try to stay on the pitch, but some post-match comments cleared things up.

When asked if his calf is ok, he told DAZN: “Yes, yes, everything’s fine, everything’s fine.” Rabiot later revealed the background to the substitution to Sky, admitting that he played a hand in convincing the coach.

“Gonçalo is the first player to do a lot. Today I saw he had a bit of pain in his thigh. I know he’s a very important player for us, and we have a lot of matches. I even asked the coach to let him rest a bit,” the Frenchman mentioned.

Speaking to DAZN after the final whistle, Amorim was asked why he felt it was right for Cisse to come on rather than Francesco Camarda, the only other natural centre-forward in the squad.

“We didn’t spend many minutes near the penalty area; he was behind. Today we were 40 metres from the goal, and Cisse was perfect for that. That’s why I didn’t bring on Camarda for Ramos: I needed someone who could run in behind.”.

#221758. Breaking: £329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham

📅 12 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 21m • 📚 Deep Dive (4114 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: £329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham

📅 12 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4114 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on fresh players really does take some doing.
  • “Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium.
  • A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on fresh players really does take some doing.

“Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

Sources indicate that for Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he remarked. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”.

Industry observers note that indeed he co-opted the Italian term “sbloccare” to describe his team’s problem. They simply need to unlock – or unblock – the team and the goals would flow. He joked that in Italy he would be lauded for two consecutive clean sheets in this game and the previous one against Nottingham Forest. “What did you write?” he demanded of one of the Italian newspaper correspondents. “You have the passport.”.

Recent findings suggest that spurs have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa, to end the streak in September. They were into the second half before the first attempt on target that obliged Jordan Pickford to make a save – Mateus Fernandes’s shot slapping limply against the Everton goalkeeper’s gloves to ironic cheers from the home fans.

At the end De Zerbi could not contain his frustration, unable to wait until he reached the privacy of the dressing room to tell Mathys Tel where he had gone wrong. He did so with the Spurs substitute still wiping the sweat from his brow on the pitch. The player did not look at all impressed. De Zerbi said later that he was simply reminding his player of what it took to play as a central striker.

“There is a term in Italian, ‘sbloccare’ that literally translates as ‘unblock’… I know we can score goals and win games. We have to respect the history of the players – if you forget [Dominic] Solanke and [Omar] Marmoush the others haven’t scored many in their careers. I think we can find the goals with the quality of the players.”.

Spurs play Liverpool at Anfield in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday before Villa a week today. The Spurs record at home is dismal. In the last 35 games they have won just five, drawn 10 and lost a remarkable 20. This latest stadium has become a problem for the team in it – or maybe it is the other way around.

Industry observers note that A good result for Everton, who were under pressure for most of the first half but had much the better of it after the break. David Moyes’s team finished the game with more shots on target than the home team. Moyes managed the game well and trusted his team to withstand the Spurs possession in the first half until they reached a point where Everton could start to push back.

Hard to pick out any major chances – it was that kind of game – but Brennan Johnson should have won it for the away team in the second half. The ball was cut back to him by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and the former Spurs man skied his shot.

Some surprised faces then when Moyes said later that he had expected a lot more from his team. He acknowledged the resilience in defence and the importance of the clean sheet. “We played well enough,” he said, “but when we had the ball we turned it over more often than we should have done.”.

According to recent reports, the game had started with Vitaliy Mykolenko being tortured by the pace of Sávio and ended with the Ukrainian left-back being given the man of the match award. Like many of his team-mates, he had hung in there. There was another fine performance from Jarrad Branthwaite at centre-half and Moyes noted that he hoped it might earn him a place in the England squad. “He is still finding his way back from injury,” Moyes said, “it would be great if he could get a call-up.”.

Recent findings suggest that in the directors’ box were the usual pained expressions of Vinai Venkatesham, the Spurs chief executive, and chairman Peter Charrington. They sat alongside Vivienne Lewis, daughter of the patriarch Joe. There is a certain fatigue about the home crowd when faced with afternoons like this which suggests they have seen so much that the bar is quite high – or low – to provoke a really splenetic response. Perhaps it is just too early in the season although the final whistle was met with boos.

The first shot on target of the entire game for either side was a free-kick struck by James Garner in added time at the end of the first half. Spurs had started at a ferocious pace although they could not sustain it.

Industry observers note that de Zerbi complained about the pre-season injuries on tour in Australia and also the lack of time he had to integrate Sávio and Marmoush. He said that his team were not in the right “physical condition”.

It has been revealed that “We played very well in the first 30 minutes and maybe the energy and the fact we didn’t score – we lost confidence.” By the end, he had sent on James Maddison, Tel, Lucas Bergvall and Mohammed Kudus to little avail. Everton looked more likely to win it.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Everton defender mentioned: “You look at the game from the start, they put us under pressure and we had to dig deep to stay in the game. Then we grew into the game towards the end of the first half and demonstrated that mentality again in the second half.

“We had chances to win the game as well. The backs to the wall mentality will help us go a long way. If we can keep clean sheets, you can go a long way in the league. But it’s not just us the defenders. It’s the whole team working hard. It’s a team effort.”.

"I feel like we could've taken three points" James Tarkowski speaks after his sides draw with Spurs 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/Wdj3N5hk8l.

Sources indicate that "Six hours and we've not scored a goal? It's a DISGRACE" 😬Ashley Young notes that the Spurs players will need to have conversations about their lack of threat going forward ❌ pic.twitter.com/0KNomGEavx.

"Absolutely diabolical" 😬Jamie Redknapp on Spurs not scoring in their first four Premier League games 😳 pic.twitter.com/48Nbxymlev.

It has been revealed that tottenham failed to take the attacking initiative or create any notable chances. De Zerbi used multiple forward players in a host of attacking positions, but no one could find the breakthrough.

Sources indicate that boos ring around the ground as Spurs and Everton both have to settle for a point. Tottenham’s winless start to the season continues, while Everton’s unbeaten run remains intact. Spurs haven’t managed a goal in six hours of Premier League football across the 2026-27 campaign. Tottenham sit 17th with two points. Everton are up to seventh and will certainly take the draw.

FULL-TIME: The points are shared between Spurs and Everton at Tottenham Hotspur stadium 🤝 pic.twitter.com/HwPuKI3Ajh.

Dewsbury-Hall’s deflected effort flies out for a corner. Everton can’t make the most of the resulting set piece and Tottenham survive.

In a recent development, there will be three minutes of added time. Are we set for late drama at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium?

Recent findings suggest that pickford makes an error as his poor clearance is intercepted by Maddison. The ball is eventually worked to Bergvall, whose curling effort is parried away by the Everton goalkeeper.

Jordan Pickford gets down well to deny Lucas Bergvall! 🧤 pic.twitter.com/59uoHTqto6.

Tosin comes on for his Spurs debut as he replaces Gray. Can anyone be Tottenham’s hero and find a late winner?

Industry observers note that garner is booked after he clatters into Savio. Everton have produced a tough and disciplined defensive perfomance so far.

Spurs are now enjoying a sustained period of possession. They’re waiting to fashion a massive chance and end their wait for a top-flight goal in the 2026-27 season.

Sources indicate that de Zerbi makes another change as Maddison enters the action with applause from the Spurs faithful. He replaces Marmoush. It looks like Tel is now operating as a false nine.

In a recent development, johnson misses a huge chance! Dewsbury-Hall fires a low cross into his path and Johnson takes the chance with a first-time shot, but he slices his effort and it goes over the bar. He’s got to do better from that range inside the penalty area.

Industry observers note that that opportunity is Johnson’s last action of the match as he comes off for Hackney. O’Brien is also introduced, replacing Maitland-Niles.

In a recent development, that was the chance. Dewsbury-Hall rolls it into the path of Spurs’ Europa League final winner Brennan Johnson and he skied it. He hasn’t scored since he left Spurs in January for Palace.

"What a chance this was!"Brennan Johnson had the chance to put Everton in front against his former club 😯 pic.twitter.com/fUi7t6hX7t.

Recent findings suggest that everton look like the far likelier side to break the deadlock. De Zerbi’s changes have done little to affect the game. Marmoush is cutting a very frustrated figure up top for Spurs.

Bergvall finds Savio with a whipped cross. The winger tries to help the ball back into the danger zone, but Pickford reacts rapidly and collects possession.

Dewsbury-Hall picks up the game’s first yellow card after catching Tonali with a late sliding challenge.

Industry observers note that what is Kinsky doing?! The goalkeeper’s dreadful pass which was intended for Tonali is intercepted by Dewsbury-Hall, who tries to slide a low effort through Kinsky’s legs. The Tottenham man redeems himself with a crucial save to keep the scoreline goalless. The hosts are living so dangerously. Kinsky needs to wake up.

Industry observers note that antonín Kinský redeems himself after Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall fails to take advantage! 😮 pic.twitter.com/nuKZju90Wz.

Moyes responds with a straight swap on the wing as Grealish comes on for George.

In a recent development, enter: Grealish. He is on for Tyrique George. Surprised that Brennan Johnson survived that change. He has struggled to make an impression.

Following Spurs’ reshuffle, it looks like Savio will stay out wide on the right, with Tel on the left. Kudus will sit as the central playmaker behind Marmoush, who is now the lone frontman.

De Zerbi orders a much-needed triple change as Kudus, Tel and Bergvall replace Solanke, Fernandes and Bentancur.

Jack Grealish has long since stopped the warm-up on the touchline and is now just staring at the game in expectation of his introduction.

A couple of chances for Everton. Spurs have survived but they look so vulnerable when Everton turn over possession. Crowd could turn soon. Almost reached the hour-mark on matchday 4 and still no Spurs’ Premier League goal.

It has been revealed that the start of Spurs’ second-half performance is alarmingly similar to their display against Newcastle two weeks ago. That day, Tottenham allowed Newcastle to seize the initiative and they netted two second-half goals without reply. Everton are gaining confidence as Spurs continue to lack courage or threat. The crowd is getting more and more restless.

Sources indicate that tottenham fail to clear a corner and the ball lands at George’s feet. The Everton winger shoots but his fierce drive is blocked by Bentancur. The whole of Spurs’ bench is warming up. The visitors currently have the momentum and the hosts look nervous.

Everton are looking threatening once again as George attempts to thread a pass through to Johnson on the counter-attack, but Van de Ven is there to clear.

George does brilliantly to escape away from Gray and floats a cross towards the back post. Barry rises highest and his close-range header is blocked by Kinsky. The Tottenham goalkeeper didn’t know much about it, but that’s a massive stop. Undoubtedly the game’s most dangerous moment in front of goal so far.

Spurs’ first shot has arrived! Unfortunately, Fernandes’ tame long-range effort is easily gathered by Pickford. There were some sarcastic cheers from the Tottenham fans as Fernandes took aim. They clearly want more attacking inspiration from their players.

According to recent reports, ironic cheers as Spurs have their first shot on target. It has taken them until the start of the second half and it would be hard to say Fernandes stung the palms of Pickford.

In a recent development, we are back under way for the second half. Everton and Spurs are both unchanged at the break. With the anxiety building in the stadium as the game remains goalless, how long will De Zerbi wait before making a change?

Recent findings suggest that an uneventful first half of football comes to a close. In a game lacking rhythm, creativity and attacking spark, nothing separates Tottenham and Everton at the break. Spurs’ search for a first Premier League goal this season continues.

There will be two added minutes. Everton have a free kick on the edge of Spurs’ penalty area. Garner and Dewsbury-Hall are standing over it. The former Manchester United and Nottingham Forest midfielder takes it and his effort bounces in front of Kinsky, who pushes it out for a corner.

James Garner free-kick pushed away by Kinsky is the game’s first attempt on target.

According to recent reports, there has not been a single attempt on target at 40:27 from either team. Spurs have had the best of it but even so. That’s a poor return.

Sources indicate that another attack fizzles out for Spurs. Substitute Jack Grealish engaging in some badinage with home fans as he warms up. He famously agreed a move to Spurs in 2018, called off at the eleventh hour when Aston Villa were sold to the current ownership.

That is so poor from Fernandes. The summer signing’s overhit corner drifts out for a goal kick. Suddenly, Spurs’ attacking play has fallen quite flat.

Pickford does well to intercept Robertson’s inviting low cross. The left back needed Solanke or Marmoush to make a darting near-post run there to give him more options.

Spurs are bossing this game but on the rare occasions Everton escape you do wonder if they might score.

According to recent reports, tottenham are roared on by the home support to move the ball a bit quicker going forward. Out of possession, Everton almost revert to a back five, with Garner dropping very deep near to Tarkowski and Branthwaite.

Recent findings suggest that tonali picks out Gray with a pinpoint pass. Garner is alert to the danger and tracks back to clear, stopping Gray from getting a one-on-one opportunity.

Maitland-Niles does very well to dispossess Tonali in a dangerous area, allowing Barry to tee up Dewsbury-Hall, but his shot is smothered by the Spurs defence. Mykolenko then chips a cross into a box, but it’s tapped behind for a corner by Robertson. Moyes will certainly be encouraged by this side’s resurgence over the last 10 minutes.

There is a break in play here with Gray down and receiving treatment after a collision. He appears to be holding his lower back. The Tottenham man gingerly gets back to his feet and trudges off the pitch.

Gray down for some extended treatment. Richarlison in the stands. Spurs in danger of losing early momentum.

After Spurs’ fast start, Everton have grown into the contest over the last five minutes and are getting on the ball far higher up the pitch.

Garner’s corner is cleared by Spurs, but only as far as Maitland-Niles. In similar range to where he scored that stunning equaliser against Manchester United, the former Arsenal man shoots, but his attempt fizzes well wide.

Industry observers note that spurs are really flowing here. Finding the balls through the lines and real speed when they attack Everton. Big question is whether they can convert that into goals. Van Hecke and Fernandes both had chances.

Recent findings suggest that sávio has had a fine start to the game. Mykolenko in for a long afternoon. Spurs have looked dangerous and should be 1-0 up.

Recent findings suggest that tonali finds Savio with a deep cross, leaving Pickford in no-man’s land. The Brazilian keeps the ball in play and it loops up, just out of Marmoush’s reach.

Robertson floats a teasing delivery into Van Hecke at the back post, but the centre-back directs his half-volley over the bar from close range.

Spurs then burst forward again through Savio, who feeds Fernandes. The playmaker’s low drive is heroically blocked by Tarkowski as Everton continue to hold on (just about).

As expected, it’s Tottenham with all the early possession, with Everton sitting very deep and soaking up the early pressure. Marmoush turns Armstrong and wins a free-kick in a dangerous area.

They’re under way in north London, the hosts are in their lily-white and navy kit, with Everton in their grey/dirty green (is that a colour?!) away number.

Greetings from N17. It’s a wonderful, warm late summer evening. As expected there is the usual foreboding from the home fans. Two defeats and one draw. The mood will sour further if Spurs do not win today. No Porro or Udogie so Archie Gray, ever adaptable, starts at right-back again.

Everton are undefeated with five points from three games. They have a decent 16/17 players but it is the reserves beyond that which everyone is concerned about. Grealish and Dibling on the bench give them two potential game-changers. Spurs’ squad looks very strong on the team-sheet. A full bench of experienced pros and no fillers. On the pitch it has been less convincing.

"Solanke is a crucial player"Roberto De Zerbi on the importance of Dominic Solanke being fit for Spurs 💪 pic.twitter.com/FNWNsTWdt8.

Ready to go 🔋 pic.twitter.com/dFb8UyiZOl.

Brennan Johnson spent two years at Tottenham and scored the winning goal in the 1-0 Europa League final victory over Manchester United in May 2025, ending the club’s 17-year trophy drought.

After a short, disappointing spell at Crystal Palace, Johnson joined Everton last month, with Dwight McNeil moving in the opposite direction.

The Welsh winger starts for Everton today. Could he hurt his previous employers on a day where they desperately need a win?

It has been revealed that brennan in the building. 💙 pic.twitter.com/94GgAY8c56.

Midfielder took exception to negativity surrounding club after moves for players on deadline day failed to materialise.

It has been revealed that “We signed Jack [Grealish], which was nice, and I’d been speaking to him,” claims Dewsbury-Hall, sitting in a café at the club’s Finch Farm training base. “But I had seen all the stuff [online], all the meltdowns about this and that and, in all honestly, it annoyed me a bit.

“I get where people are coming from. Everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad, but there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded. I was seeing people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’.

According to recent reports, “What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go. That’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room.”.

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

The winger only made his debut for Tottenham as a late substitute against Nottingham Forest last week, but his attempt to rebuild his career following his anti-doping ban has been dealt a major blow.

Folarin Balogun’s proposed £39m move from Monaco collapsed on transfer deadline day, Richarlison’s return to the club didn’t materialise and Beto was sold to Fiorentina, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton’s only recognised striker.

Nottingham Forest’s pursuit of academy product Harrison Armstrong ruffled the fans’ feathers, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City for £60m.

Dwight McNeil, Tim Iroegbunam, Nathan Patterson, Adam Aznou and Idrissa Gueye were also allowed to leave.

Merlin Rohl and Tyrique George made their loans permanent, while Brennan Johnson, Hayden Hackney and Christian Norgaard were also added to the squad.

Summer signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Vitaliy Mykolenko are David Moyes’ only options at full-back.

Overall, there were a number of solid additions, just not enough of them to cover all the departures.

In a recent development, 🎧🫡 Thierno Barry ahead of today's clash in North London. pic.twitter.com/mwlsKH8Pid.

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van de Ven, Van Hecke, Robertson; Tonali, Bentancur, Fernandes; Savio, Solankem, Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Tel, Bergvall, Kudus, Davies.

Everton: Pickford; Maitland-Niles, Tarkowski, Brathwaite, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry.

Subs: Travers, O’Brien, Keane, King, Alcaraz, Graham, Hackney, Dibling, Grealish.

After scoring that last-minute leveller against Manchester United last time out, Ainsley Maitland-Niles is promoted to the starting 11 and replaces Merlin Rohl. Brennan Johnson returns to his former club and starts, while Jack Grealish is on the bench.

Today's Toffees to face @SpursOfficial. COYB! ✊#TOTEVE pic.twitter.com/mOcCayRUfm.

Roberto De Zerbi has made four alterations from last weekend’s stalemate with Nottingham Forest. Dominic Solanke, Mateus Fernandes, Archie Gray and Andy Robertson all come into the line-up. Pedro Porro and Destiny Udogie are out injured, while Conor Gallagher and Mathys Tel are relegated to the bench. Tosin Adarabioyo and James Maddison are also among the substitutes.

Our Spurs side to take on Everton 👊🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/n637s7swiD.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Everton in the capital.

Sources indicate that are Tottenham in must-win territory already? It may seem reactionary and premature, but after spending £380m in the summer to revamp an underperforming squad, Tottenham sit inside the relegation zone, with just one point and zero goals scored in three games.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men opened the 2026-27 top-flight season with worrying back-to-back defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, before ending their losing streak last weekend thanks to a goalless draw against Nottingham Forest.

This game gives Tottenham another opportunity to reverse their dreadful home form. Last season, Spurs managed just three league wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and lost 10. The recent 2-0 loss against Newcastle was a painful reminder of Spurs’ shortcomings at home, but they’ll be expected to be authoritative and seize the initiative here today. A much-needed three points would be the perfect remedy to ease the pressure and unwanted attention on De Zerbi and his squad.

Meanwhile, Everton have made an unbeaten start to the season, accumulating five points from their first three league matches. David Moyes’ side looked set for defeat last time out, when they were trailing Manchester United 2-1 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium heading into stoppage time, until Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ stunning 96th-minute equaliser salvaged a draw.

Alongside drama on the pitch, there has also been noise off it. A bizarre transfer window has left Everton with a serious lack of depth up top and in both full-back positions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to the fans’ negativity over this situation, saying their meltdowns “annoyed” him.

Nevertheless, they arrive in North London with all eyes on Tottenham and if the hosts can find a first league victory this season.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

Leicester City could lose loan star in January as parent club consider recall

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (529 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that leicester City sit 7th in League One ahead of this weekend’s clash with Mansfield Town.
  • Sources indicate that form has picked up in recent weeks but as the January window gets closer, talk of departures has ramped up.
  • Howell has featured primarily from the bench in League One this season, making just the one start.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that leicester City sit 7th in League One ahead of this weekend’s clash with Mansfield Town. Russell Martin’s side have picked up 23 points from 15 matches, winning six, drawing five and losing four.

Sources indicate that form has picked up in recent weeks but as the January window gets closer, talk of departures has ramped up. One of which could be loanee Harry Howell, who Brighton are considering recalling from LCFC, according to Pete O’Rourke.

Howell has featured primarily from the bench in League One this season, making just the one start. In all competitions he has two goal contributions in 13 games for the Foxes.

It has been revealed that brighton are considering a recall to send Howell elsewhere in January in a bid to get more game-time. A host of clubs both in England and across Europe are keen on the 18-year-old.

Howell’s loan spell at LCFC has so far failed to provide the regular senior football Brighton wanted for his development. The 18-year-old England U19 international joined the League One club in August to gain valuable first-team experience after limited opportunities at the Amex.

Martin has acknowledged Howell’s restricted role, explaining that illness disrupted his early progress. The attacking midfielder initially made a positive impression before a virus affected his fitness and forced the club to manage his minutes carefully.

By the time he returned, Leicester had established a rhythm and altered their formation, leaving Howell struggling to find a suitable place in the side.

Industry observers note that there have been encouraging signs when given opportunities, including a league goal and promising contributions from the bench in the FA Cup. However, the overall lack of playing time means the loan has fallen short of its primary objective.

Howell was intended to be a key player for Leicester City this season but for a multitude of reasons that has not happened. With that in mind, it is no surprise that Brighton are considering moving him on.

Sources indicate that however, that should not be a real issue for LCFC for the rest of the season. The Foxes have plenty of options in that area, with the likes of Kamari Doyle and Sammy Braybrooke currently in fine form.

Losing loanee Howell may mean that Leicester can go out and bring in another loanee in January with a squad spot opening up. With players like Conor Chaplin, Tommy Watson and Liam Cullen also in the squad, they can likely afford to bring in a play in another area instead of a direct replacement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that female mosquitoes use several sensory systems to locate a host whose blood they can feed on. One of these systems is a group of proteins known as ionotropic receptors, which detect the acidic compounds in human sweat that contribute to its sour smell. Writing in Nature, Xu et al.1 report 3D structures of an ionotropic-receptor complex from the malaria-spreading mosquito Anopheles stephensi. The structures show how the binding of an acid activates the receptor, which then opens its ion-conducting pore and generates an electrical signal that helps to guide the mosquito towards a human host.

David Raya's shoulder injury isn't 'too serious', confirms Mikel Arteta - as relieved Arsenal boss reveals stricken goalkeeper won't need surgery and COULD face Manchester City

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1118 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 09:10 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:39 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Mikel Arteta said David Raya’s shoulder injury isn’t ‘too serious’, sparking hope that the goalkeeper could return within weeks.
  • Raya was forced off in the 70th minute of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw against Newcastle on Saturday at St James’ Park, hurting his left shoulder in a collision with William Osula.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By ISAAN KHAN, REPORTER and WILL GRIFFEE.

Published: 09:10 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:39 EST, 24 November 2026.

Mikel Arteta said David Raya’s shoulder injury isn’t ‘too serious’, sparking hope that the goalkeeper could return within weeks.

Raya was forced off in the 70th minute of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw against Newcastle on Saturday at St James’ Park, hurting his left shoulder in a collision with William Osula. He looked in agony as he left the pitch.

His No 2 Kepa Arrizabalaga is instead expected to play for the north London club in their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday.

Though Arteta confirmed Raya doesn’t require surgery and didn’t yet rule him out for Sunday’s Premier League clash against Manchester City.

‘He’s (Raya) not fit for tomorrow, but it doesn’t look too serious,’ remarked Arteta. ‘We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. It seems to be better than expected.

‘We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had. The first test shows something much more encouraging.

Arsenal's No 1 David Raya underwent an MRI scan the day after going off against Newcastle.

‘There is no need for surgery, which was the main fear because that would have ruled him out for months.’.

Asked whether Raya could play at home to Man City, he added: ‘Tomorrow we’ll have more tests and we will know. I think we’ve seen what David brings to the team as well.

‘That’s why we are very protective with Kepa and (third-choice) Illan (Meslier). Everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen.’.

Raya has been sensational for the Premier League champions and his absence is likely to hurt the best defensive unit.

'That's a massive worry,' Ian Wright mentioned on Sky Sports when the stopper went down. 'I don't want to say I'm petrified simply because Kepa is in goal, he's the guy who has got to try and keep the goals out for us now.

'But yeah, that is a massive blow. Someone like him, Declan Rice, Gabriel, it is very tough to replace those guys.'.

Meanwhile, Bruno Guimaraes said Arteta is ‘crazy’ about the small details that will take him to ‘another level’.

Since his summer move from Newcastle, the 29-year-old has scored vital goals against Sunderland and Leeds - but is yet to complete a full 90 minutes in the Premier League.

Raya hit the turf in pain and went off the pitch clutching his arm to indicate that something serious had happened.

‘I now definitely understand my role in the team and the way Mikel wants me to play but I can still play much better,’ mentioned the Brazilian.

According to recent reports, ‘I think Mikel (Arteta) is unbelievable. He as a manager is so focused on small details, the way you control the ball, the way that you cannot be aligned with your opposite side.

‘Some details I have never heard before, I just found out with him here. He is crazy a little bit about these small details and I try and take (in) as much as I can because he is so passionate about them.

Sources indicate that ‘He highlighted me some clips (from when I was) in Newcastle and some clips here, where he thinks I can do things differently. He's trying to take me to another level.’.

Arsenal's clash with Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night will feature a fresh innovation for its TV audience watching on Prime Video. Called 'Progressive Actions' it highlights the passes and ball carries that drive a team up the pitch, and the often-unsung players behind them. Developed by Prime Video's team of producers, engineers, AI experts, and on-air analysts, Progressive Actions is the first Prime Insight built specifically for the UEFA Champions League. It joins the growing suite of features on Prime Vision, the alternate feed which serves as a laboratory and incubator for new features that often advance to the main broadcast.

Sources indicate that progressive Actions is built on proprietary AI-powered models that identify a Progressive Action based on how far the ball travels in each phase of the pitch, with the threshold becoming shorter closer to the opposition goal where defences are more compact and space is harder to find. The metric mirrors the data used behind the scenes at Europe's elite clubs, yet has historically been difficult to show during a live broadcast. As a player makes a Progressive Action, an on-pitch graphic will show where the action started and ended, the player involved, and the distance the ball advanced, allowing fans to see the game as a coaching team would, in real time.

'Prime Vision is where we develop fresh features that shine a spotlight on the metrics, actions and players that impact a game most, yet aren't always captured by traditional statistics or broadcast techniques,' noted Andrew Hornett, Director of Live Sports Production for Europe at Prime Video.

'Every team has players whose influence goes far beyond the scoresheet, the ones doing the crucial work in the build-up, moving the ball forward two or three passes before an assist. Progressive Actions is designed to capture that impact, measuring and visualising these actions during a live broadcast. Fans will see them in real time as they happen, but we'll also aggregate the data across the game, so you can see which players have had the biggest impact on the match.'.

Industry observers note that the feature will debut in the UK and Ireland on Tuesday and will also be available for fans in Germany and Italy. Fans can access Prime Vision, with features including Progressive Actions, via their remote from the match detail page or the in-game menu during any live UCL fixture on Prime Video.

Progressive Actions is the first Prime Insight built from the ground up specifically for Prime Video's UEFA Champions League coverage, and sits alongside Tactical Map, Momentum, Physical Insights, Advanced Analytics, Passing Options, and Player ID in Prime Vision's growing suite of features designed to take football fans closer to the game, all available on the alternate feed during every UEFA Champions League match live on Prime Video. Prime Insights were first developed for Prime Video's coverage of Thursday Night Football, its exclusive weekly NFL package in the US, where AI-powered features including the award-winning Defensive Alerts have become a staple of the coverage, advancing from the alternate feed to the main broadcast each week.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that birmingham City sit 4th in the league after 17 matches and they are not showing signs of slowing down.
  • The most impressive part of Blues’ resurgence this season is their away form, as they have already matched their away win total from last season – and it is only November.
  • In a recent development, this was a huge reason that Chris Davies‘ side fell short of reaching the Championship play-offs last season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that birmingham City sit 4th in the league after 17 matches and they are not showing signs of slowing down. BCFC won comfortably against a poor Burnley side last night to take their tally for the season to 32 points.

The most impressive part of Blues’ resurgence this season is their away form, as they have already matched their away win total from last season – and it is only November.

In a recent development, this was a huge reason that Chris Davies‘ side fell short of reaching the Championship play-offs last season. A significant part of the improvements on the road this term has been the defence. The Blues have conceded the fewest goals in the Championship and kept a sixth clean sheet of the season against Burnley.

According to recent reports, on Wednesday, they did so without captain and standout centre-back Christoph Klarer due to suspension. With Dael Fry alongside Phil Neumann, Birmingham City looked just as solid at the back.

There were some questions over how the Blues would handle missing their captain against Burnley after he picked up a suspension against Stoke City. However, Dael Fry was an ideal replacement for Klarer.

Industry observers note that fry has struggled for game time since leaving Middlesbrough. He hadn’t started in the league up until Birmingham City’s match at Turf Moor.

Industry observers note that the 29-year-old has had to bide his time due to Klarer and Neumann forming such a strong partnership this season, and despite this, Fry slotted into the backline perfectly. The former Boro mainstay provided the physicality and no-nonsense defending to make him an ideal partner for Neumann’s speed and ball-playing ability.

Industry observers note that fry was a force in both boxes as he constantly won headers in attack and defence. He won three of his five duels total and was assured in possession with 41 passes completed, seven of which were into the final third (FotMob). He showed that despite his lack of game time, he is still a top defender at the level.

BCFC were praised for signing Fry on a free in the summer due to his experience, and he looks as though he will still have an crucial role to play in the Blues’ promotion push this season.

Birmingham City have had to make a lot of changes this season due to injuries and suspensions. However, they have looked strong no matter who is playing.

It has been revealed that there was a clear focus on depth in the summer window. So far, at points, Carlos Vicente, Paik Seung-ho, Max Bird, Ryan Allsop, Ethan Laird and Dael Fry have all had to come in the starting lineup to replace first-choice players this season.

Having top Championship players like coming in as backup options is a huge weapon for the Blues. Fry would be the first choice at centre-back for a lot of sides in this league.

This depth could really help Birmingham City in a promotion push this season, but it gives Davies a tough call on how best to manage Fry, as a player of his quality is sure to be eager to play more football.

Fry is a professional who can contribute away from the pitch, but his quality is clear to see, and it deserves to be on show. Davies will be more than aware of this, and he will simply encourage the player to prove he deserves to find more minutes when the chances arise.

Frosinone head coach Massimiliano Alvini has admitted that his side simply gave AC Milan too many opportunities.

Recent findings suggest that it has been a very positive return to the top flight for Frosinone so far, given that a point last night at San Siro would have seen them move back into the European places. However, they were ultimately given a bit of a humbling by Milan, who won 5-1 thanks to a ruthless counter-attacking display.

It has been revealed that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Some have questioned if the Canarini were a bit too aggressive in their approach to the game, given they played with such a high line and allowed space for Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to exploit.

Industry observers note that alvini was present in the press conference room at San Siro after the full-time whistle and he analysed what was perhaps the most difficult night of the season for his team. MilanNews transcribed his assessments.

Should the game have been played differently?

“Frosinone played their game but made a few mistakes they don’t usually make, but that’s certainly not my concern, losing by such a large margin. What’s worrying are the mistakes we made that we could have avoided.”.

It has been revealed that “We made a mistake on the first goal, which was a mistake of our own, while the other goals we conceded were goals we absolutely could have avoided. We conceded them and were naive.

“It’s a mistake of our own, and so today, from this perspective, if you come to Milan against Milan and make these mistakes, it’s only natural that we end up losing like this, by such a large scoreline.

“That’s the analysis, even though I think the scoreline is even too large: the first half, in my opinion, was extraordinary on our part.”.

Did the absences have an impact, forcing you to experiment a bit?

“There’s nothing experimental about it. We played with the same principles, running forward to get to Rabiot. We preferred to bring on a defender who would push forward rather than a midfielder.

“In my opinion, this definitely didn’t influence the result, but rather the attitude, the idea, or the match strategy. And we certainly made – as I said before and I’ll repeat – mistakes we don’t usually make.

“If you give Milan certain chances, with such strong players and the quality of this team, you risk losing, and that’s what happened. You risk losing with a heavy defeat, and that’s what happened.

It has been revealed that “He had a problem with that back heel in the box, and he definitely needs tests. It’s too early now; we’ll have to wait for the tests, which will be done starting Tuesday, but it’s definitely a problem.”.

“We had a chance with Monterisi after a minute, we hit the post, and we created a lot. I have nothing to say to the team for their attitude and the way they played.

“We, I repeat, made some naivety, some mistakes. It’s also up to me to understand that there are important players on the other side who can cause problems.”.

In a recent development, “It’s a result that definitely needs to be managed, navigated, and channeled, but it doesn’t change my attitude at all. We have 20 points today. The path we need to take is to try to stay in Serie A, and we’ll try to do so with this attitude, with this identity: this is the path we’ll take.

“Four years ago, I drew a game against Milan by playing defensively, and we took home a point. Today we made some mistakes, but this is the path we’ll take. I’m happier with the management, with the team’s identity, to try to achieve that objective, and this is what we’ll continue to do.”.
