Manchester United are reportedly considering a move for Borussia Dortmund attacker Mathis Albert during next summer’s transfer window.

The 17-year-old joined Dortmund’s youth academy from LA Galaxy in 2024, and he has progressed to the first team at BVB, making four appearances.

Albert has only made three appearances for Dortmund this season, and it is understood that he is not presently happy with his playing time at the club.

According to Sky Deutschland, a switch during the January transfer window is not being ruled out, but a move to Old Trafford next summer is viewed as a possibility.

The report claims that fresh Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is a huge admirer of Albert and could push for his arrival in 2027.

Albert played under Pochettino for the USA, scoring once in five caps.

Pochettino’s arrival at Old Trafford has allegedly strengthened Man United’s chances of signing Albert, but the Red Devils are not the only club in the running for his signature.

Albert is primarily a left-sided attacker, but he is also capable of playing down the right or as a second striker.

The 5ft 10in forward had an excellent record for Dortmund’s Under-19s, scoring 14 goals and registering nine assists in 30 appearances.

Three of his four appearances for Dortmund have come in the Bundesliga, but he is yet to feature in the Champions League.

Man United are planning to be busy during the January transfer window, with the club presently struggling towards the bottom of the Premier League table.

A new centre-back is high on Man United's wish-list, with Brentford's Nathan Collins and Fulham's Calvin Bassey both believed to be potential options at the start of 2027.

The 20-time English champions would also like to bring in a upcoming centre-forward, but the club allegedly only have a £50m budget for the January window.

55 min: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 0 A fantastic save from David Raya, who springs to his left and touches Enzo Le Fee’s penalty onto the post! Sensational goalkeeping!

Enzo Le Fée is denied by David Raya from the spot 😳🧤📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/wnoMCDVh88.

54 min: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 0 A long throw from the left is claimed by David Raya - but the referee points to the spot after a wrestling manoeuvre by Konsa on Ballard!

Arsenal are furious, and that probably wouldn’t have been given last season, but clubs were told at the start of the season that wrestling would be penalised.

In a recent development, gabriel goes down holding his jaw and claims he was elbowed by Ballard. VAR aren’t interested and the referee tells an irritated Gabriel to leave the field for one minute.

Konsa makes an vital challenge on the relentless Brobbey, as does Gabriel on Le Fee a few seconds later. Sunderland keep pushing and Sadiki rakes a shot over the bar from the edge of the area.

Chance for Sunderland A long throw from the right isn’t cleared by Arsenal, and eventually Meunier hits a snapshot that is kicked away instinctively by David Raya. That’s a pretty good save.

We’re off again at the Stadium of Light.

Jurrien Timber and Bruno Guimaraes, who is popular in these parts, replace Ben White and Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Tzolis’s deep cross is headed back into the six-yard box by Saka. Havertz stoops towards the ball but is beaten to it by Xhaka, a crucial bit of defending and the last action of a hard-fought, goalless first half.

Ben White has a groin problem and is going to be replaced by Jurrien Timber, either now or at half-time.

It has been revealed that xhaka’s dangerous corner is punched back to him by Raya. He picks out Le Fee, who drags a shot wide of the near post from 20 yards. Sunderland’s belief is growing.

Angulo goes down in the Arsenal area after a challenge from the side by White. Play continues and Meunier’s speuclative shot deflects behind for a corner.

Sunderland have been terrific in this first half.

Mikel Arteta is booked for encroaching outside his technical area. He responds by sticking his thumb up at the fourth official.

Mikel Arteta receives a yellow card for stepping out of the technical area 😅📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/xDlnL1B9MY.

Arsenal are yet to score from a set piece this season. Their supporters have used that fact as evidence they are not as reliant on corners as their critics say, but the truth is that it will bother Arteta and set-piece coach Nicolas Jover. This is the sort of cagey game in which Arsenal so often made the breakthrough from a set piece last season.

Sunderland break through Mukiele, who charges into space and rifles a low drive that is blocked by Gabriel on the edge of the area.

The resulting corner leads to a brief VAR check for an Arsenal penalty after a bit of a wrestling match between Calafiori and Brobbey. Nothing given.

Good save by Roefs Saka curls a cross towards Havertz, who does well to control it on the chest while facing away from goal. He waits for the ball to bounce and hooks an imaginative shot that is fingertipped over by Roefs. Good save.

Chance for Arsenal Tzolis plays a nice pass down the side of the area for Odegaard. He cuts the ball back to Havertz, who screws a first-time shot over the bar. It was a slightly awkward chance because of the angle of Odegaard’s pass.

In a recent development, reinildo is booked for a foul on Saka. The home fans are getting annoyed with what they perceive as diving from some of the Arsenal attackers: “Same old Arsenal, always cheating” is the chant of choice just now. Odegaard also went down a moment ago after a foul from Angulo.

Gabriel strides forward from defence and sweeps a left-foot shot from 25 yards. It’s a good effort that fades just wide of the far post with Roefs scrambling across his line.

According to recent reports, sunderland will be really pleased with the first quarter. They’re defending solidly and look a threat on the break, thanks in part to some outstanding hold-up play from Brian Brobbey. Saka’s volley is the only shot on target at either end.

Recent findings suggest that chance for Sunderland Brobbey does brilliantly to hold the ball and find Le Fee, who is fouled on the left wing by Gabriel. That allows Sunderland to send the centre-backs forward - and one of them, Dan Ballard, almost opens the scoring!

Xhaka curled a sensational ball around the Arsenal defence towards the far post, where the ball bounced up awkwardly and was knocked wide by either Ballard or Mukiele, who flew in at the far post. Ballard would have had an easier chance had Mukiele not got in the way.

It has been revealed that chance for Arsenal Saka mishits a volley straight at Roefs from close range after running onto a penetrative pass from Rice. It wasn’t an easy ball to take on the volley - Rice hit it very firmly - but Saka would usually do better.

The pattern of the game has been established, with Arsenal dominating the ball and Sunderland picking their moments to press and then counter-attack.

Looks like it will be a good battle between Brian Brobbey and Ezri Konsa. Brobbey seems to be attaching himself to Konsa, rather than getting into a scrap with Gabriel.

Sources indicate that sunderland break promisingly down the right. Mukiele drives an angled low cross that only just evades Angulo at the far post.

Calafiori has a shot from 18 yards blocked after a typical run infield from left-back.

Industry observers note that enzo Le Fee tries to score from inside his own half. David Raya was outside the penalty area but Le Fee completely mishit the shot.

Industry observers note that arsenal have started well and are dominating possession. So far it’s all been in front of the Sunderland defence, but you’d expect that to change if they continue to have this much of the ball.

The champions kick off from left to right as we watch.

There’s a pulsating atmosphere at the Stadium of Light - you’d expect nothing less - and the action is about to begin.

Myles Lewis Skelly is the first England teenager to start the first four league games of a season for Arsenal since Tony Adams and David Rocastle in the 1986/87 campaign.

In a recent development, we’re in a congested period right now. We’re playing midweek games as well. We made four changes against Napoli, we make another four for today and we try to keep all the players connected with a high level of confidence, and with the right chemistry in and around the team.

We know how tough Sunderland made it for every opponent here [last season] and we know the beautiful atmosphere that they create, the organisation that they have and the individuals that they have. We’ll try to impose ourselves like we always do and come here and be as dominant as we’ve been and then be ready to win the game.

According to recent reports, arsenal’s biggest rivals are still waiting for their first win - and their first goal - of the Premier League season. Alex Connor has reaction to their 0-0 draw at home to Everton.

"For sure we can improve, and we will" 😅Mikel Arteta on Arsenal's strong start to the season 🗣️📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nDpwooZq4Y.

Arsenal keeper David Raya has conceded only one goal in five matches this season, but he was beaten twice on this ground last season during a thrilling 2-2 draw.

It has been revealed that when will Martin Zubimendi start again for Arsenal? Mikel Arteta wants to avoid a repeat of last season, when Zubimendi played more games than anyone in Europe, but it is curious that the Spaniard has not yet started a single match of this campaign. It is one thing to reduce his minutes, and another to turn him into a permanent substitute.

Zubimendi has looked quite good off the bench in recent games but has been behind Myles Lewis-Skelly and Mikel Merino in the battle to partner Declan Rice from the start. And that’s before Bruno Guimaraes, the fresh £75m signing, reaches full fitness.

According to recent reports, in the thick Naples air in midweek, Declan Rice did what he always does: he kept running. Another start for the Arsenal midfielder, another 90 minutes completed and another performance of constructive passing and destructive defending. For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

After that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that the key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. This, after all, is a footballer who managed nerve pain in his hamstring throughout the second half of last season.

Regis Le Bris, who made 11 changes for the League Cup win over Hull in midweek, reverts to the starting XI that drew at Brentford seven days ago.

Industry observers note that RLB's XI to take on Arsenal! ❤️👊#SUNARS pic.twitter.com/F1nXWky4Fp.

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the Arsenal team that won in Napoli during the week. Kai Havertz’s return is the headline news in Arteta’s selection, with in-form left-back Riccardo Calafiori also returning. Myles Lewis-Skelly returns to the midfield and Christos Tzolis starts.

🟡 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🔵 Your Saturday night Gunners ❤️‍🔥🤝 Presented by @deel.

Hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

There’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

It has been revealed that “I love those challenges,” said Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

Industry observers note that “Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”.

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”.

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

Maritimo vs Nacional - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Maritimo and Nacional renew their Madeira derby rivalry in the Primeira Liga on Friday evening, with both sides looking to claim an important victory and move further clear of the drop zone.
  • The two clubs are meeting in the top flight for the first time in five years, with the visitors sitting 13th in the Primeira Liga table on 10 points from 11 matches, just two points above the 15th-placed hosts, who have a game in hand against Estoril Praia and sit outside the relegation playoff place on head-to-head points ahead of Casa Pia.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 25 Nov 2026 16:48.

Maritimo and Nacional renew their Madeira derby rivalry in the Primeira Liga on Friday evening, with both sides looking to claim an important victory and move further clear of the drop zone.

The two clubs are meeting in the top flight for the first time in five years, with the visitors sitting 13th in the Primeira Liga table on 10 points from 11 matches, just two points above the 15th-placed hosts, who have a game in hand against Estoril Praia and sit outside the relegation playoff place on head-to-head points ahead of Casa Pia.

Maritimo made an encouraging start to life back in the top flight, winning their opening two league fixtures against Casa Pia and Famalicao, but they have not claimed another Primeira Liga victory since beating the latter on August 16.

Mitchell van der Gaag's side have since gone eight league matches without a win (D2, L6), including defeats in their last three such outings against Porto (2-1), Vitoria de Guimaraes (5-0) and Santa Clara (2-0).

Only bottom-placed Estoril, who are yet to win a league match this season, have endured a longer winless run, while Maritimo have scored the third-fewest goals in the division (nine) and conceded the third-most (21).

Van der Gaag's men have also struggled to make home advantage count, recording just one victory from five league matches at their own ground and losing the last three, during which they conceded multiple goals on each occasion and scored just once.

Maritimo did, however, receive a welcome boost in the Taca de Portugal last weekend, progressing past Chaves following a goalless draw and a 3-2 penalty shootout victory, and will hope that result provides some momentum ahead of Friday's derby.

Nacional have also endured a difficult start to the campaign, but they have collected six points from their last three matches, including a 1-0 victory over Academico de Viseu courtesy of Matchoi Djalo's late winner.

That result marked the first victory under upcoming boss Joao Henriques, who arrived in late October as the club's third permanent manager of the season following the departures of Joao Giao and Alexandre Santos.

Henriques initially struggled to build on interim coach Bruno Abreu's home victory over Braga, losing away to Arouca in his first match in charge, but the latest success has given the Alvinegros an opportunity to record consecutive competitive wins for the first time since beating Alverca and Tondela in April.

Interestingly, Nacional's last four matches have each produced just one goal, including their disappointing Taca de Portugal defeat to lower-division Sanjoanense on October 17, meaning taking maximum points on Friday could hinge on greater efficiency in attack and defensive discipline.

However, the Islanders still have plenty of room for improvement away from home, having collected just one point from five Primeira Liga trips this season, drawing at Santa Clara on the opening weekend before losing their next four against Vitoria, Sporting, Rio Ave and Arouca.

Nacional have also found this fixture difficult in recent meetings, losing four of their last five league encounters with Maritimo across the Primeira Liga and Liga 2 (D1), including a 3-1 defeat on their most recent competitive visit.

Maritimo form (all competitions):.

Nacional form (all competitions):.

Maritimo are monitoring defenders Rafael Fernandes (muscle) and Paulo Henrique (thigh), who both missed last weekend's cup tie against Chaves.

Yellu Santiago is also working his way back to full fitness from an injury, having only featured in the opening weekend of the Primeira Liga campaign.

Goncal Tabuaco's performance against Chaves has given Van der Gaag a decision to make in goal after he replaced Fran Vieites in the cup, saving two penalties during the shootout.

Nacional will be without Ulisses Wilson and Filipe Soares, who are both recovering from ankle injuries and remain unavailable.

Leo Santos (knee) is also sidelined, while Brazilian duo Wesley Gasolina and Liziero continue to recover from their respective injuries.

Henriques could retain the lineup that started against Viseu, with Miguel Baeza anchoring the midfield, although Djalo is pushing for a starting place after making an impact from the bench last time out.

Maritimo possible starting lineup:.

Vieites; Igor Juliao, Correia, Szalai; Tavares, Andrade, Guzzo, Ogbeta; Bassouamina, Butzke Tejon.

Nacional possible starting lineup:.

Marin; Jensen, Goncalves, Vitor, Kokolo; Baeza, Dias, Djalo; Labidi, Njoya, Song.

Maritimo have struggled to turn home advantage into league points this season, but Nacional's poor away record gives the hosts reason to believe they can avoid defeat, making a share of the spoils a reasonable prediction.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The 20-year-old could leave Old Trafford to find more game time, be it on loan or a permanent basis, and the Hammers are monitoring his situation.
  • However, his need to play could force the issue and bring a January move to fruition.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham boss Scott Parker is determined to bolster his ranks in the winter transfer window. A striker and a left-back is on the WHUFC chief’s radar, and reports have noted there is an interest in Manchester United’s Ayden Heaven too.

The 20-year-old could leave Old Trafford to find more game time, be it on loan or a permanent basis, and the Hammers are monitoring his situation. According to The Athletic, Heaven is keen to play more, but his true desire is to stay at Manchester United, fight for his place in the team and help their battle to rise out of the Premier League relegation zone.

However, his need to play could force the issue and bring a January move to fruition. Premier League clubs have made contact to gauge Heaven’s availability and there may be a decision to make over his future in the coming weeks.

Heaven started his academy career in the West Ham setup, leaving in 2019 to join Arsenal. He cemented himself as one to watch while with Arsenal, but a desire to find more first-team opportunities prompted a move to Manchester United in the winter of 2025.

It has been revealed that he broke into the side under Ruben Amorim but has primarily played as a backup since. The London-born prospect is held in very high regard, but the need for immediate results at Manchester United means new boss Mauricio Pochettino would be taking a gamble in entrusting Heaven with a starting berth.

As a left-footed centre-back, Heaven is adept at progressing the ball from deep with a good passing ability and a willingness to carry the ball in dribbles. This aspect of his game was nurtured at Arsenal, and it has helped him slot in at Old Trafford.

He deals with aerial duels well for a player of his inexperience, but his limited senior game time has seen issues regarding anticipation and one-on-one defending arise. Heaven can develop in these scenarios over time though – he just needs regular exposure at first-team level.

Recent findings suggest that A drop to the Championship could benefit Heaven. He would be backed to start regularly at West Ham, likely taking Max Kilman’s place to slot in alongside Konstantinos Mavropanos at centre-back.

Industry observers note that playing in a team that wants to challenge for promotion and play possession football would make for good exposure for Heaven. However, it would not be a surprise if his sights are set higher.

In a recent development, heaven is a highly-rated prospect who has already played Premier League football, and he will be confident in his belief that he can deliver at top-flight level if entrusted with a regular role. It could make clubs in higher leagues more attractive than WHUFC, especially on a permanent basis.

The Hammers should keep track on his situation, but be aware that they could be outdone if the door does open for Heaven to move on from Old Trafford.

Watch out, AlphaFold: Claude and ChatGPT’s latest biology skills wow scientists

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (970 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Accurately predicting protein structures has been the preserve of specialist artificial-intelligence tools such as AlphaFold — but now general-purpose models are catching up.
  • According to recent reports, earlier this month, Xinming Tu set out to test what artificial-intelligence models know about proteins.
  • He left the analysis to run overnight and woke up shocked at the results.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Accurately predicting protein structures has been the preserve of specialist artificial-intelligence tools such as AlphaFold — but now general-purpose models are catching up. Credit: EMBL-EBI (CC0).

According to recent reports, earlier this month, Xinming Tu set out to test what artificial-intelligence models know about proteins. Tu, a researcher at an AI biology company called Phylo in South San Francisco, California, asked large language models (LLMs) from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google to predict the sequences of obscure bacterial proteins.

He left the analysis to run overnight and woke up shocked at the results. The latest versions of Anthropic’s Claude models had outperformed other LLMs — including specialized protein-language models, which are trained on vast troves of sequence data and designed for such tasks.

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary new proteins.

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary latest proteins.

It has been revealed that when Tu and Leo Chen, a computational biologist at Harvard Medical School in Boston, Massachusetts, shared the results in a 16 November blog post, it set off a frenzy among computational biologists to see what other protein biology LLMs such as Claude could do. For instance, Tu, Chen and others have found that the tool could perform a key step in protein-structure prediction.

In a recent development, and on 24 November, OpenAI confirmed that its latest language models had successfully designed new proteins, some of which behaved as expected when they were made and tested in the laboratory. The results hint that the latest LLMs might be gaining a sophisticated understanding of protein biology.

The research has kicked off a debate over the future of biological AI. Some scientists predict that ‘general purpose’ models such as Claude and ChatGPT will eventually outperform specialist tools such as AlphaFold at tasks including protein-structure prediction and design.

“We want to see a world where a scientist can just describe in natural language what they want a ChatGPT model to do, and the model can just be infinitely flexible and design exactly what the person wants,” indicates Joy Jiao, who leads life-sciences research at OpenAI in San Francisco, California.

In a recent development, but some researchers question the extent to which LLMs are learning underlying lessons in protein biology. They suggest that some of the models’ abilities could be the result of regurgitating training data.

Industry observers note that the unveiling of AlphaFold2, Google DeepMind’s blockbuster AI tool for protein-structure prediction, in 2020, launched a revolution in biological AI. There is now a vast ecosystem of software — much of it open source — for modelling different properties of proteins, such as how they interact with potential drugs, and for designing latest proteins.

In a recent development, researchers have begun using LLMs to orchestrate these specialist models, but the LLMs have been used mostly as a time-saving measure, claims Martin Pačesa, a structural biologist at the University of Zurich in Switzerland. “In most cases, a specialist will always perform better than a generalist for a given task,” he says.

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI.

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI.

To see if an LLM could stand in for specialist protein-design tools, Jiao and her colleagues asked an OpenAI model called GPT-6.2 to design 3D protein structures capable of binding to five biological targets, including proteins implicated in cancer and immune conditions. After the LLMs generated the designs, the researchers used a specialist AI tool to determine a corresponding genetic sequence. Lab experiments confirmed that around 11% of designs were able to bind to their target.

Recent findings suggest that in other experiments, the OpenAI team indicated that its LLMs could design protein sequences, redesign existing antibodies, and do other tasks typically performed by specialist tools. In some cases, the LLM performed as well as some specialist tools, and in others, such as predicting the 3D structure of proteins, it was far off. OpenAI researchers describe the work in a blog post and technical paper.

Jiao emphasizes that the work is a proof of principle, and that specialized AI tools were still needed for key steps. But Masatoshi Uehara, an OpenAI researcher who was part of the effort, thinks that LLMs will only get better at protein biology. “I believe the large language model can technically beat every specialized model in each capability,” he notes.

O'Neill believes Kieran Tierney is close to the form that earned him a £25m move to Arsenal.

Champions League contenders PSG and Bayern Munich face contrasting attacking crises ahead of crucial tests

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1075 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 17:05.
  • Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich enter Wednesday's Champions League fixtures facing significant questions about their attacking strength, with injuries forcing Luis Enrique and Vincent Kompany to reconsider how their teams operate.
  • Recent findings suggest that the reigning European champions host Roma without Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, two of the players most responsible for providing individual creativity in Luis Enrique's fluid attacking system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 17:05.

Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich enter Wednesday's Champions League fixtures facing significant questions about their attacking strength, with injuries forcing Luis Enrique and Vincent Kompany to reconsider how their teams operate.

Recent findings suggest that the reigning European champions host Roma without Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, two of the players most responsible for providing individual creativity in Luis Enrique's fluid attacking system. Bayern, meanwhile, travel to Lille without Harry Kane, whose influence extends well beyond his remarkable goalscoring record.

According to recent reports, both clubs remain among the contenders for the European title, but the nature of their problems differs considerably. PSG must compensate for losing two players capable of creating advantages from wide positions, while Bayern are missing the central figure around whom much of their attacking play has been organised.

Their circumstances are also different in the league phase. Paris have won all four matches and collected 12 points, while Bayern sit 13th with eight points following two victories and two draws. Wednesday's matches will provide the first European examination of how both sides respond to their recent setbacks.

According to recent reports, PSG's problems began on October 20, when Kvaratskhelia suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury during the 4-2 victory over Barcelona. The Georgian subsequently underwent surgery, leaving Luis Enrique without one of his most effective players in one-on-one situations.

It has been revealed that the situation worsened on Saturday when Doue sustained a similar injury during the 3-2 Ligue 1 win at Nice. The France international had scored earlier in the match but was forced off before half time and now faces an extended recovery period.

The absence of both players removes two key sources of creativity from an attack built around movement, positional exchanges and the ability to beat defenders individually.

It has been revealed that kvaratskhelia's influence is particularly apparent on the left, where his dribbling and ability to move inside create space for overlapping teammates. Doue offers a different range of solutions, operating from the right while frequently drifting into central positions to combine with midfielders or attack the penalty area.

Losing both simultaneously could make PSG's attacking patterns easier for opponents to anticipate, particularly when facing teams prepared to defend in a compact shape.

Luis Enrique still has considerable resources. Ousmane Dembele is available after returning from a hamstring injury, while Maghnes Akliouche, Ferran Torres and Mika Godts provide options across the attacking line. However, finding an effective combination is likely to require more than simply replacing the two injured players with others occupying the same positions.

The Spaniard has nevertheless rejected suggestions that PSG must respond immediately in the transfer market.

Industry observers note that "We don't need to sign players in the transfer window," Luis Enrique said ahead of the Roma encounter. "It's not our style to sign a player for just six months. We're happy with our squad.".

He also emphasised the resilience his team have demonstrated in recent seasons, insisting that the injuries would not diminish their ambitions.

It has been revealed that wednesday's meeting with Gian Piero Gasperini's Roma presents a particularly demanding test. The Italian coach favours aggressive defending and a flexible tactical approach, potentially challenging PSG's ability to progress through central areas without relying so heavily on their absent wingers.

Gasperini acknowledged the significance of the injuries but warned against underestimating Paris.

"PSG are a proper team and can also make up for the absences of very good players with their own organisation," he noted during his pre-match press conference.

For Luis Enrique, maintaining that collective identity while introducing new attacking combinations will be essential to PSG's hopes of challenging for a third successive European crown.

Bayern's immediate problem is concentrated through the middle of their attack, where Kane's absence has removed the team's most influential forward.

According to recent reports, the England captain suffered a syndesmosis ligament injury during Friday's 1-1 Bundesliga draw with Cologne and subsequently underwent surgery. He is expected to miss several months, depriving Kompany of a player who had already contributed 10 goals and 10 assists in 16 appearances this season.

Those figures illustrate the difficulty of replacing Kane. His value lies in his ability to drop into midfield, connect attacks and create space for teammates, as well as his finishing inside the penalty area.

A conventional replacement might occupy the same central position without providing the passing range and movement that allow Bayern's wide players to attack the spaces Kane creates.

It has been revealed that kompany's options have been further reduced by the absence of Ismael Saibari, who is recovering from an ankle injury, and Serge Gnabry. Michael Olise has also been ruled out of the Lille fixture with a foot problem, removing another significant source of creativity and attacking production.

In a recent development, there is some encouragement in the return of Luis Diaz, who is available again after a minor hamstring injury, while Jamal Musiala is working his way back towards full fitness. Neither development, however, eliminates the challenge of reorganising an attack that has relied heavily on Kane's contribution.

Bayern sporting director Max Eberl acknowledged that the team would need to adapt its approach.

According to recent reports, "The dynamic of our play must change to an extent," Eberl told the club's official website. "We have to try with the team to defend well over the whole game and score the required goals.".

Kompany has similarly focused on the players available rather than those missing, describing the situation as exceptional but insisting that Bayern retain enough quality to compete.

"It's a chance to get wins in a different way," the Belgian said. "Now we have to show energy and mentality.".

In a recent development, unlike PSG, Bayern have less room for error in the league-phase standings. Their eight points leave them outside the top eight places that guarantee direct qualification for the last 16, making the visit to Lille crucial beyond its tactical implications.

Sources indicate that the two Champions League contenders therefore approach Wednesday with different priorities. PSG must preserve the variety of their wide attacking play, while Bayern need to establish a newly introduced way of creating and finishing chances without Kane.

The performances against Roma and Lille will offer an early indication of which adjustments are effective, although neither match alone can establish how the injuries will shape the remainder of their European campaigns.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.
  • It has been revealed that but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

It has been revealed that but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

According to recent reports, united were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent massive players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

Sources indicate that they hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

Recent findings suggest that the question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

Recent findings suggest that it was telling that so little did City’s upcoming head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Recent findings suggest that maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a substantial team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

There was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL.

Sources indicate that and the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Industry observers note that patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the glitch then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

It has been revealed that united can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

Industry observers note that “We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

Recent findings suggest that I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

In a recent development, the decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but big moments in games like that have a big impact.

We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

Industry observers note that we could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the strategy of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

[On Foden’s red card] Can be a red card, but in the same action can be a red card for Bruno. It is what it is, we won.

Changed the proposal for us, and changed the plan for them. They are unbelievable in transition, and the moment we are with 10 men we give them no transitions.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

We always knew it was going to be a tough game. What happened with Phil at the start wasn’t good for us, but we said at half-time it would make us feel better if we win and we’ve taken three points.

Sources indicate that it just gives you more motivation to go on and get the points. It was really tough for us. We had to run more and fight more. We all shone, to a man, and we were brilliant.

He was offside and what I can’t understand is it’s the rules... I went there because he was in front of him because that’s why Haaland was free at the back.

Every season they come to our club and spend an hour and a half explaining the rules, and they seem so confident with that, and then you have five or six people making this mistake. It’s unacceptable.

We have to go home with this injustice.

Industry observers note that haaland speaking on Sky: “We had to go low which is not ideal, we like to keep the ball, to try to score goals but in these times you have to go a bit low and take your chances when possible. We managed to do that well and that indicates personality and character, to keep the ball away at Old Trafford with 10 men.”.

Sources indicate that “We had to change the plan a bit, but Enzo gave us a plan where we could play to our different strengths and counter-attack a bit more. For me personally, I just had to be there, to try to wait for a chance, and if there’s a chance, I had to be ready to execute. We also needed fighters in the team, which we have plenty of. Look at our midfield - it’s something they like to do! I’m so, so proud of everyone.”.

And on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”.

City win the Old Trafford derby with 10 men and Enzo Maresca runs down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling fans while their players embrace Donnarumma after his late save.

In a recent development, there will be so much analysis of Foden’s red card, but more so how Haaland’s winner stood given the final result. Should Enzo Fernandez have been considered offside?

But if you are judging performances, City are worthy winners. They defended stoutly, carried a threat and kept the ball well for periods even though they were a man light. United were aimless and froze.

A mammoth victory, and one which perhaps puts the breaks on talk of an Arsenal procession.

In a recent development, what a chance for Mbeumo to equalise! Superb save by Donnarumma, after the United forward was found by a Bruno Fernandes disguised pass into the box. Mbeumo took the ball under his spell and shot with power, but the big goalkeeper pushed the shot over the bar.

United have a corner, but Michael Oliver blows for a foul, and that is surely that.

Martinez tries a straight ball towards Sesko, which is too high for the striker. United have perhaps just one more attack in them if they are too salvage a point.

Dalot with another poor cross that flies over everyone in the penalty area. Then Mainoo’s pass in midfield is intercepted by Anderson, and Ndiaye can bring the ball forward for City until he his tackled buy Martinez.

Fernandes drifts a cross behind for a City goal kick, between Sesko and Zirkzee and it looks like United are running out of time and ideas.

In a recent development, dorgu with another foul on Ndiaye, yet another break in play for City. And there are going to just FIVE minutes of added time, much to Old Trafford’s frustration.

Haaland does well to bring City forward after another United attack breaks down, and Dorgu is penalised for a foul on Ndiaye. Another stoppage follows because the ball hits Michael Oliver. City can see the finish line so, and they would deserve their three points.

United have a corner after Guehi stands firm to block Cunha’s strike from distance. Maguire rises highest in the middle, but no United player gambled on the knockdown and his header drifts wide of the post.

Good work from Anderson against Mainoo in midfield, he receives a substantial cheer from the City fans. Carrick has thrown attackers on, but United have lost some structure and are not sustaining pressure.

Nico O’Reilly is now on for the closing stages, in place of Fernandez and Carrick has thrown on Zirkzee in place of Marcus Rashford. A United goal now would feel like a goal out of nowhere. City are playing the better football now and they have a corner.

United have lost all sense of momentum, City are keeping the ball for spells and then are happy for the game to be broken up stoppages.

Sources indicate that fernandez goes down looking for a penalty rather hopefully, and Maguire has been booked for his reaction as well as Fernandez for his role in the fracas. More and more time ticks away.

Recent findings suggest that city are showing real resolve as well as quality here, Enzo Fernandez has just won a free-kick in the United half after a foul by Mainoo. The closest United have come in recent minutes was a glancing header wide from Mbeumo.

From that free-kick, Fernandez’s low delivery is close to being converted by Haaland or Guehi.

It’s a big final 16 minutes here plus injuries for United. You’re at home to your derby rivals who have been down to 10 men since the 23rd minute and you’ve had just two players show up for the mostpart so far - Mainoo and Rashford. The rest are really going to have to lift it.

Fernandes stings the palms of Donnarumma with a strike from outside the box.

The VAR check for offside on Haaland found that he was in fact onside by fine margins, and that Fernandez (who was offside) did not affect Lisandro Martinez as he threw himself at a diving header (and missed). The Fernandez element feels the more debatable.

United get the first Manchester derby of the season under way.

Plumes of red and green and yellow smoke filled the air as fans brandished banners and flags and chanted anti-Glazer and Ratcliffe songs.

Enzo Maresca has selected the more attacking option by playing Enzo Fernandez deeper alongside Elliot Anderson, rather than pushing the Argentine up a line and starting O’Reilly or Bouaddi. Still no Doku for City, and Foden has been preferred to Ndiaye out wide.

They are now 2-0 down against Brighton and Taiwo Awoniyi has been sent off for an elbow. Bar a miracle, it will be zero points from four games for Frank Lampard’s team.

Recent findings suggest that there will be no flags in the Stretford End today in a protest against ticketing policy which United say is about stopping touts, but loyal, innocent fans may have been caught in the crossfire. A crackdown has led to 685 supporters being stripped of their season tickets and another 464 being sanctioned. Fans will unfurl a giant banner reading “The Way You Treat Us Is A Disgrace” aimed at the club’s hierarchy this afternoon. You can read more here from James Ducker.

Both of these teams were in Champions League action this week but, as James Ducker explores in this piece, United have missed out in six of the last 13 campaigns. City have been ever-presents, with significant sporting and financial benefits. Over the 10 years between 2016 and 2025, City generated £343m more in broadcast revenue and prize money from European football than their derby rivals.

In a recent development, sam Wallace was at Carrington this week to speak with Diogo Dalot, the Manchester United right-back who could make his 250th appearance for the club this afternoon. Dalot has been through some tumultuous times at Old Trafford, and is one of the great survivors in the squad. He talks about the scrutiny at United, his musical family and the negatives of social media for young players in an interview you can read here.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

According to recent reports, to most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

Rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very important in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

Sources indicate that it has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

With Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Maresca’s team have had lots of the ball in their first few games of the season, so that is the expected pattern again.Full team news on the way later.

Last night, AC Milan watched their former midfielder Franck Kessie help their top four chances and even their Scudetto hopes.

Recent findings suggest that after a 5-1 win at San Siro, things couldn’t have got much better for Milan last night. Yet, somehow, they did. Indeed, the late kick-off on Sunday saw Atalanta host Inter and it seemed that the Nerazzurri were heading for another three points, having gone 4-2 up.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, a brace from Charles De Ketelaere – the second coming to make it 4-3 – and a late penalty from Kessie levelled the scoring and meant Inter stayed within two points of the Rossoneri.

Speaking to DAZN after his late equaliser, Kessie admitted that he still saw the game as a derby, even if he’s no longer a Rossoneri representative, as MilanPress relayed.

In a recent development, “We have great faith in coach Sarri and his staff. The season is still long. Tonight we responded strongly. A heavy penalty at the end? You can score or miss: it went well. For me, it was a small derby against Inter: thank goodness I scored… ”.

Given what it means for the title race, the Diavolo will thank the Ivorian for his contribution and if he plays a part in another successful season, he’ll only be thanked more for it.

Man City's controversial orange kit sparks fan criticism as Premier League restriction emerges

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (865 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 17:29.
  • Manchester City's decision to wear a striking orange fourth kit during Tuesday's Champions League draw with Napoli has drawn criticism from supporter groups, while Premier League regulations mean the controversial shirt cannot be worn in domestic league matches.
  • According to recent reports, the Citizens abandoned their traditional sky-blue colours for the 2-2 encounter at the Etihad Stadium, unveiling a special-edition strip created by Puma and Italian fashion brand C.P.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 17:29.

Manchester City's decision to wear a striking orange fourth kit during Tuesday's Champions League draw with Napoli has drawn criticism from supporter groups, while Premier League regulations mean the controversial shirt cannot be worn in domestic league matches.

According to recent reports, the Citizens abandoned their traditional sky-blue colours for the 2-2 encounter at the Etihad Stadium, unveiling a special-edition strip created by Puma and Italian fashion brand C.P. Organization. The launch formed part of a commercial collaboration, with the collection scheduled to go on sale worldwide on December 1.

Sources indicate that the decision proved divisive, particularly as Enzo Maresca's side extended their winless run to five matches. According to Brazilian outlet Trivela, two independent supporter organisations have questioned the timing of the initiative and its apparent prioritisation of commercial interests.

In a recent development, there is also a regulatory complication. City have already registered their three regular kits for the 2026-27 Premier League campaign, meaning their newly introduced orange design cannot be added to the selection of strips available for league fixtures.

Premier League clubs are permitted to use a maximum of three registered outfield kits during a season, normally comprising their home, away and third-choice designs.

City have already filled those places with their traditional sky-blue home strip, a black-and-yellow away kit and a predominantly white third shirt featuring blue detailing.

Their newly introduced orange shirt therefore falls outside the competition's permitted selection, regardless of whether the club wishes to use it again.

The restriction is not related to the unusual colour, the shirt's design or its association with C.P. Manufacturer. It follows from the fact that City have introduced an additional strip beyond the three registered for Premier League use.

UEFA's kit regulations operate differently, allowing clubs greater flexibility over the number of approved designs they can wear in European competition.

That explains why City were able to introduce the orange shirt against Napoli and could use it again during selected Champions League fixtures later this season.

The club confirmed the arrangement in an official statement following Tuesday's match, describing the outfit as a special-edition collaboration with Puma and C.P. Tech giant.

Supporters will have an opportunity to purchase items from the collection at an exclusive pre-sale event at the City Store in Medlock Square on November 30, before the worldwide release the following day.

The FA Cup could also provide another opportunity to wear the shirt, although its use would require the appropriate approval from the Football Association.

It has been revealed that such exceptions are not unprecedented. Arsenal received permission to wear a special white kit in the FA Cup as part of their No More Red initiative, which raises awareness of knife crime and youth violence in London.

The Premier League restriction is only one aspect of the controversy surrounding City's latest release.

According to Trivela, the Citizens Trust, an independent supporter organisation established earlier this year, criticised the decision to introduce the orange shirt and expressed opposition to initiatives perceived as explicitly promoting third-party commercial interests.

Another independent organisation, the 1894 Group, reportedly raised concerns about the club's priorities, arguing that City should be concentrating on strengthening their relationship with supporters during a difficult period.

Those objections are particularly relevant because the latest kit made its debut at the Etihad, where City would ordinarily wear their familiar sky-blue colours.

In a recent development, the orange design has no obvious connection to that traditional home identity. However, C.P. Company has a longstanding association with British football terrace fashion, and its partnership with City dates back to 2024.

The club therefore has a cultural and commercial rationale for the collaboration, even if some supporters remain unconvinced by its appearance on the pitch.

Tuesday's result did little to improve the mood. City were held to a 2-2 draw by Napoli despite a late equaliser from Rayan Cherki, extending a difficult run for Maresca and his players.

The manager is already facing questions about his team's performances ahead of Sunday's Premier League trip to Arsenal, making the timing of a high-profile commercial launch a particularly sensitive concern.

City have previously demonstrated that fourth kits can generate interest without provoking the same debate over their relationship with the club's identity.

Their 2024-25 special-edition shirt, developed with Noel Gallagher, celebrated the 30th anniversary of Oasis's debut album, Definitely Maybe.

The design drew on the Manchester band's history and Gallagher's longstanding support for City. It was worn during Champions League fixtures against Inter Milan and Paris Saint-Germain.

In a recent development, the latest collaboration follows a different approach, reflecting C.P. Company's influence on football fashion rather than a specific event from the club's own history.

There is no indication that City intend to withdraw the orange kit following the criticism. Their official announcement identifies it as an outfit for selected European fixtures, and the commercial launch remains scheduled for next week.

Recent findings suggest that for supporters attending Premier League matches, however, there will be no repeat of Tuesday's unusual appearance. City's three registered domestic kits will remain the available options, leaving the orange shirt as a feature of their European campaign.

By Darren Plant | 25 Nov 2026 17:37.

Oliver Glasner has outlined how Nottingham Forest must improve during Friday's Premier League fixture against Chelsea.

However, there is an argument that Xabi Alonso's Blues are suffering from the same problems as their East Midlands hosts.

Forest head into their upcoming game sitting in 17th position in the Premier League table, seven points adrift of their eighth-placed opponents.

While Forest's underlying statistics in the final third have been encouraging, individual mistakes have sometimes cost them.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference, Glasner acknowledged that Forest's players must perform better in many areas of their game.

The Austrian told reporters: "We’ve been talking a lot about running here. You can see we’ve climbed the bottom of the table. We are starting to be in mid-table with all these stats. I think we can see this progression.

In a recent development, "The physical – especially the running stats – are getting more and more competitive. You don’t need to be a heavyweight boxer in our squad. But you need to anticipate. You need to be quick in legs and in mind.".

When addressing other problems, he added: "We all thought and wished we would have more points. Performances in many games were better than results. We wanted and expected more from us to be honest.

"We have to accept the reality. I’m no magician. I have no magic dust I can spread. We need to improve our individual mistakes.

According to recent reports, "We need to improve our efficiency in attack. Still no goals from set pieces. I think I always talked about stability and consistency. This is what we still have to find and do better.

"To really perform consistently on a high level, we get enough points and we get enough wins. Then you climb the table and this is what we’re looking for.".

After the 4-1 defeat at home to Leeds United, Alonso gave a dismissive answer when a reporter claimed that Chelsea were unable to cope physically against the majority of Premier League teams.

However, it has been clear to supporters that Chelsea possess a team that struggle on that front, with decision-making and in front of goal.

Add in the frequent individual mistakes and you get a similar team to Forest, albeit one that is less physically-imposing.

There is an argument that Chelsea are the perfect opponents for Forest to return to form.

Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

📅 14 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5352 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half.
  • Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins.
  • There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

“Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

Sources indicate that “I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “But this was a top-class performance.”.

Recent findings suggest that it has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

In a recent development, the home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj.

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a substantial evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

It has been revealed that massive? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

In a recent development, leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Recent findings suggest that ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO.

Leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9.

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

According to recent reports, A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x.

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

“That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”.

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

[It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

Industry observers note that it’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

[Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

Exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No.

For each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

According to recent reports, energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

We have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

According to recent reports, [Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

In a recent development, the ref told me at half-time that they’ve taken it off me. I didn’t know he [Bogle] was there to be fair. I just got up and went ‘Bang!’ It is what it is. I’ll take the assist!

Industry observers note that I didn’t know anything about it [being given credit for the second goal]. I said to the ref, I don’t fancy telling him [Calvert-Lewin]. To be fair he’s still raging. He’s raging with the goal but happy with the result.

It’s about having an understanding with the players around you. With Dom up there, you know he’s going to win everything so you have to get the runners around him.

Recent findings suggest that it’s about the rotation like today. When James Justin goes wider there’s space inside. Dom occupies two centre-backs so there’s always pockets.

Regardless of the scoreline it was a tough game physically. They’re a very good side. We take it game by game, not to get carried away. Everyone’s ambitious in their own way but we have to take it game by game.

A proper stuffing for Newcastle as Leeds continue to impress and climb up to third.

James pounces on a loose ball, dribbles infield from the right. No one bothers to close him down so he eventually has a shot, blazing over with his left from 20 yards.

Late free-kick for Leeds after Livramento bundled Aaronson over. Wilson chips from the left to the far post and Muharemovic heads it back acros goal looking for a team-mate but none had made the run.

Leeds 4 Newcastle 1 (Touré) No clean sheet for Leeds. Farke is fuming after the substitute exploits an error and scores with a left-foot shot that deflects off Justin.

Anthony [Elanga] is injured. Unfortunately we have to investigate further how long he will be out but obviously we miss him. We wish him to come back as quickly as possible. It could be [a long-term injury] but he will get another MRI next week and then we’ll see.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

But Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

Jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

According to recent reports, there are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

This is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

He formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the latest boy Fernandez-Pardo?

Sources indicate that mind you I remember his visit to Elland Road in 1982-83. Not for the faint hearted. In fact it was a disgrace when he was hit by a coin. And yet he was always gracious about Leeds and particularly fond of Don Revie. He was one of very few football people without a strong Leeds United connection who went to his funeral in 1989.

Apparently he was injured in training, the nature of the injury is unspecified.

Industry observers note that newcastle have made a very good start particularly in their transitional moments on the counter-attack. We have to be switched on today to get the next points.

Recent findings suggest that after many years of suffering our supporters deserve it [high expectations]. It’s good but we are far away from not being humble. Our feet are on the ground. We know the second year is always difficult. We have made a good start and it is always important to ride the momentum as long as possible.

Eddie Howe has left a legacy and the culture he created is still around. Matthias has to work with it. They are unbeaten. they are very dangerous with many pacy players up front. It’s important not to lose the ball too easily and always be switched on against Newcastle.
