Recent findings suggest that good evening and welcome to live coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United, the last Premier League match of the fourth round of fixtures for the 2026-27 season. Both clubs have made unbeaten starts with one win and two draws each and a win today for wither would send them up to fourth. The two sides met at Elland Road in the third match of last season which ended in a 0-0 draw but the return fixture at St James’ Park was one of the games of the season, a ding-dong match that Leeds led 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, the latter until the 91st minute and yet still lost 4-3.

It has been revealed that the architect of that victory for Newcastle was the Leeds’ fans’ incubus, a player commonly known around Elland Road as ‘Harvey F------- Barnes’. His two goals that night were his sixth and seventh against Leeds in eight matches for Leicester and the Toon. Back in the last century and at the turn of this one, Alan Shearer scored 21 league goals in 23 games against Leeds for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle, it can feel like one bogeyman passing the baton to another.

Industry observers note that newcastle’s sound form with their latest model team this season has been based on searing pace and their ability on the counter whether with runners, in the case of Anthony Elanga, or with long diagonals against Tottenham that ripped a hole in the left side of their defence. Leeds rallied from being overrun by Brentford at half-time in their last home game to switch from three at the back to four and wrest back the initiative and while they reverted for the Brighton draw, in both games it was the introduction of Ao Tanaka in midfield that gave them control.

It is genuinely hard to decide whether the 6-3 defeat by Chelsea in the Carabao Cup from being 2-0 up at Stamford Bridge is significant to Leeds league form. One simplistic way of looking at it would be to say Leeds reserves were better than Chelsea’s reserves in the first half and Chelsea’s first-team were better than Leeds reserves and their shaky, debutant keeper in the second. But any similar defensive frailties tonight and there will be jitters over the next week before the international break. Newcastle, by contrast, toiled in their 1-0 victory over Millwall but the result glosses over a lack of incision for long spells of it.

Joe Rodon is out for Leeds for at least another month while Newcastle have changed to withholding information about their treatment room under Matthias Jaissle who says that it should be ‘confidential’. We do know that Joelinton, William Osula and Dan Burn are likely to still be out given the nature of their injuries but Amar Dedic, who came off at half-time at the Fresh Den with a thigh or hamstring problem, may be back.

Last night, AC Milan added another five goals to their tally in Serie A, making it one of their best starts to a season ever.

Sources indicate that with Ruben Amorim, Milan are no longer the defence-first team that Massimiliano Allegri made them. Instead, they’re fluid, attacking and dangerous and the statistics show as much. So much so that their stars are shining brighter than they may have ever done before.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent development, as Gazzetta dello Sport writes, the Rossoneri are on fire, so much so that they’ve only outscored this season’s start twice in their history. With 28 goals in 12 games, everyone is helping things tick, but Pulisic, again, is standing out.

After a fine international break, the American ‘led the way’ again and added a goal to his tally for the season in fine fashion. He dons the superhero cape in a team that ‘plays, scores and has fun’ and with him, the team keep winning.

It has been revealed that every 87 minutes in the league, he’s contributed and for that reason, there’s a sense of inevitability seeing him in the teamsheet. Gazzetta writes that it’s effectively like entering every game with a 1-0 lead already.

In a recent development, he’s now scored in three consecutive games and it’s form that has not been bettered since the start of the 2024/25 season; where he scored four goals in a row. It’s not really a surprise, either.

In Ruben Amorim’s front-foot system, he’s one of the frontmen and that naturally means he’s going to score and create more. A ‘perfect match’ for Amorim, he’s leading in every sense and you’d have to look to the teams of Nereo Rocco and Lajos Czeizler for more goals – both teams scored 29 in their first 12 games of the Serie A season.

In a recent development, ardon Jashari grabbing a goal also raised the number of scorers this season to eight, which is impressive in itself. It’s a ‘super-attacking’ team where everyone contributes, but Pulisic is again leading.

Since relegation from the Premier League in 2018, Stoke City have had seven different permanent managers/head coaches, and it would be a fair assessment to say that some have done better than others.

2016 was the last time Stoke recorded a top-half finish of any division they have been in, with three ninth-placed finishes in a row in the Premier League being followed up by a decade of mediocrity and disappointment.

Right now, the Potters are flying towards the top of the league, and there is genuine hope amongst the fanbase that they can finally end their barren run this year and in style.

Stoke supporters have seen nearly everything since their relegation to the Championship, as Football League World has attempted to rank the last seven Potters managers from worst to best.

Kicking us off and the worst out of the bunch, although some will argue otherwise, is Nathan Jones.

Jones found success in his early days of management with Luton Town, helping to take the Hatters from League Two to League One, implementing his infamous 'diamond' formation, and with the Hatters flying high in the third tier in January 2019, he was poached by the Potters.

His time at the club, to put it bluntly, was horrific, losing his first two games in charge to Brentford and Shrewsbury Town, and guiding the club to a 16th-placed finish in their first year back in the Championship, as well as spending £7 million on Sam Vokes, then 29.

The free additions of the likes of Jordan Cousins, Lee Gregory, Nick Powell, Adam Davies, and Stephen Ward the following summer did little to excite supporters, and by the time November 2019 rolled around, he was dismissed with the Potters sitting at the foot of the second tier.

Six wins in 38 games managed, a win rate of just 15.79 percent, Jones is statistically the worst Stoke manager of all time to manage over 20 games, and whilst he has revived his career with Charlton Athletic, his time in the Potteries was an unmitigated disaster.

Just the third-ever manager Stoke have appointed that is from outside the British Isles, after Johan Boskamp and the late Gudjon Thordarson, Narcis Pelach arrived in North Staffordshire in September 2024 following the surprising dismissal of Steven Schumacher.

It was a major call from Jon Walters and the rest of the Stoke hierarchy, who earmarked the former Huddersfield Town and Norwich City coach as the man who could take the club in the right direction.

Unless the right direction was towards the bottom of the Championship, his time at the helm did not go to proposal, losing his first game in charge at home to Tim Walter's Hull City and doing little to convince supporters that he was the right man for the job.

Under the Spaniard, Stoke conceded shots and chances for fun, and with just three wins in 19 games across all competitions, the same win percentage as Jones (15.79 percent), incidentally, his time at the helm was as brief as it was unsuccessful.

Since his dismissal in December 2024, Pelach has been an assistant to Graham Potter at West Ham United, and now manager of Red Bull-affiliated RB Omiya Ardija in Japan.

Following Stoke's relegation to the Championship in 2018, Gary Rowett was chosen as the man to take the Potters immediately back to the Premier League, being poached from Derby County.

In excess of £50 million was spent under Rowett on the likes of Sam Clucas, James McClean, Ryan Woods, Benik Afobe, Peter Etebo, and Tom Ince, as the Potters looked to buy their way back to the top flight.

Long story short, Stoke regressed even further under Rowett, lacking any clear identity or attacking prowess despite the lucrative money spent. An away trip to Marcelo Bielsa's Leeds United on the first day of the season was possibly the worst fixture he could've hoped for, as Stoke were run off Elland Road in a 3-1 defeat.

Stoke's spending under Rowett would set the wheels in motion for the mediocre years to come, as it notes a lot that despite his excessive spending and subsequent football, he doesn't feature lower.

Alex Neil first moved to English football in January 2015 with Norwich City thanks to his excellent work in Scotland with Hamilton Academical, and guided the Canaries to the Premier League in his first six months in charge.

Spells with Preston North End and Sunderland followed, guiding the latter to promotion to the Championship in 2022, as Stoke decided to poach him from the Black Cats the following August.

He'd guide the Potters to a trademark 16th-placed finish in his first year in charge, and in the summer of 2023, he'd be allowed to stamp his authority on the club with the additions of the likes of Wouter Burger, Ryan Mmaee, Ben Pearson, Bae Jun-ho, and Lynden Gooch, amongst many more.

Three months later, Neil was dismissed following a glum 1-0 home defeat to Sheffield Wednesday with Stoke sitting just above the relegation zone, and though he has found his footing again with Millwall, the job at the bet365 Stadium proved too tough for the Scot to handle.

Replacing Neil at the helm was former Plymouth Argyle boss Steven Schumacher, who had previously helped the Pilgrims earn promotion from League One to the Championship with 101 points, and was awarded League One Manager of the Year.

Schumacher helped to guide Stoke to safety, finishing in 17th and closing out his first campaign in charge with three wins on the spin, and heading into the summer, there was excitement around the place once again.

The 42-year-old would bring in the likes of Sam Gallagher, Ben Gibson, Eric Bocat, Ashley Phillips, and Tom Cannon, but after just seven games into the season and four wins in all competitions, including a 5-0 away win against Middlesbrough, Schumacher was surprisingly dismissed.

He has since helped to guide Bolton Wanderers back to the Championship, and remains a likeable figure at Stoke, with many supporters believing he was treated unfairly by the hierarchy.

The current man at the helm, and if receny bias took control of this ranking, he would certainly be first, but looking at the bigger picture, Mark Robins can only take second spot, for now.

The former Coventry City boss took charge of Stoke in January 2025 following the dismissal of Pelach, and ultimately guided the club to safety in the Championship by the skin of their teeth.

It was November 2025 when Stoke were flying towards the top of the table, and Robins appeared to be building something special, but a calamitous drop in form, where only Sheffield Wednesday picked up fewer points than the Potters in the second half of the season, saw the club drop to 17th.

Robins retained the faith of the Stoke board over the summer, and was allowed to spend in excess of £30 million on the likes of Ethan Galbraith, Justin Devenny, Jack McGlynn, Luca Bombino, Djibril Soumare, George Hirst, and Luke Graham, and right now has the club flying.

Time will tell whether Robins writes his name in the club's history books at the end of the season, but for now, only one man can top him.

Recent findings suggest that do you agree with our rankings? If not, what would be your rankings and why? Share your thoughts below!

When Michael O'Neill was appointed as the manager of Stoke in November 2019, he joined with the club rooted to the bottom of the Championship and, alongside balancing his role at the helm of Northern Ireland, was tasked with keeping the Potters up.

A 4-2 win away against Barnsley in his first game in charge set the tone, and crucial wins over relegation rivals followed to drag Stoke away from danger, as O'Neill finished his first year in charge in 15th.

Under a watertight budget, the Northern Irishman stabilised Stoke and brought in the likes of Jacob Brown, Ben Wilmot, and Josh Laurent to the club in his three summers in charge, whilst also bringing through academy players Nathan Collins, Tyrese Campbell, and Harry Souttar.

He recorded two 14th-placed finishes in the Championship during his two full years in charge, both the best finishes the club has had in the past decade, as whilst O'Neill ultimately failed to build Stoke into a play-off-chasing side, he certainly saved them from relegation and remains a favourite in the Potteries to this day.

Alanyaspor will be looking to halt their alarming slide down the Turkish Super Lig standings when they welcome Konyaspor to GAIN Park on Friday evening.

The hosts sit 14th in the table with 12 points from 12 matches, while the visitors occupy 15th place with eight points and will be hoping to close the gap after suffering three consecutive league defeats.

Alanyaspor have endured a difficult period in recent weeks, losing five consecutive league matches and leaving themselves increasingly vulnerable to being dragged into the relegation battle.

The Thunders began that sequence with a 3-0 defeat away to Fenerbahce before suffering a 2-1 home loss against Kocaelispor six days later, and their struggles continued when they travelled to face Genclerbirligi, suffering a humiliating 5-0 defeat, which was followed by a 2-0 home loss to Trabzonspor.

Those results led to Joao Pereira leaving by mutual agreement, with Ugur Ucar subsequently appointed, but the new manager was unable to bring about an immediate improvement as Alanyaspor were beaten 2-1 at Kasimpasa in his first game in charge.

They have now lost five Super Lig matches in a row and are without a win in their last six, drawing one, leaving Ucar with plenty to address as his side attempt to rediscover the form that helped them collect points earlier in the campaign.

Their recent performances have also been particularly disappointing defensively, having conceded 12 goals across their last five league matches, making them the worst-performing side in the division over that period.

The 4-1 victory over 12 Bingolspor in the Turkish Cup is the only positive result the Thunders have recorded during that spell, and just their second home win across all competitions, having won only their opening home league game, drawn two and lost two, leaving them without a league victory on home soil in their last four attempts.

However, Alanyaspor have enjoyed the better of recent meetings between the sides, remaining unbeaten in their last six competitive encounters with Konyaspor while winning each of the last five.

Konyaspor, meanwhile, have also struggled to maintain consistency this season and are four points behind the hosts, having collected just two wins, two draws and eight defeats from their opening 12 league matches.

Ilhan Palut's side have also lost their last three league games, suffering a heavy 4-0 home defeat against Galatasaray before losing 1-0 away to Samsunspor and then 4-2 against Besiktas in their latest outing.

Aside from their poor record in this fixture, the Anatolian Eagles have another concern heading into Friday's encounter, having collected just one point from five away matches this season.

In fact, Konyaspor have failed to score in their last four away matches, losing three of those games by a 1-0 scoreline, with a goalless draw against Kasimpasa coming between those defeats.

The Anatolian side have also failed to win on their last three visits to Alanyaspor, losing the previous two by 2-1 scorelines after drawing 2-2 on their earlier trip.

Pakistani astronaut to become first foreign visitor to China’s space station

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Three astronauts will launch aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.Credit: Xinhua/Shutterstock.
  • For the first time, China will send a foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station.
  • Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani military pilot, is expected to travel to Tiangong on 25 November aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, alongside two Chinese astronauts, known as ‘taikonauts’.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three astronauts will launch aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.Credit: Xinhua/Shutterstock.

For the first time, China will send a foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station.

Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani military pilot, is expected to travel to Tiangong on 25 November aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, alongside two Chinese astronauts, known as ‘taikonauts’.

According to recent reports, “My first [flight] not only represents myself, but also my country,” Ali told reporters in Mandarin on 24 November at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China. Ali has been training intensively in Beijing for the past seven months, including learning Mandarin. He said that he carried “the dream of 250 million Pakistani people” when he entered the training centre.

Sending an astronaut to space is “a huge step” for Pakistan’s space aspirations, says Wajiha Iqbal, a lunar scientist at the University of Münster in Germany. The partnership enables Pakistan to “do great science in space”, she adds.

The mission is also a milestone for China’s space programme. The country’s expanding capabilities now allow it to offer international partners opportunities that few countries can provide on their own, says Yuxuan Jia, who researches China’s foreign policy at the Center for China and Globalization, a think tank in Beijing. The launch signals China’s “aspirations to become a top space power”, Jia says.

Recent findings suggest that shenzhou-24 is expected to be carried into a low-Earth orbit by China’s Long March-2F rocket, which is scheduled to launch from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre at 08:18am local time on 25 November, stated Zhang Jingbo, a spokesperson of the China Manned Space Programme, at a press conference on 24 November. Shenzhou-24 is expected to automatically dock with Tiangong (which translates as ‘heavenly palace’) around 3.5 hours after reaching orbit.

Ali will stay on Tiangong for about a week before returning to Earth with two of the three taikonauts right now on the station.

China’s successful launch of Mars mission seals global era in deep-space exploration.

China’s successful launch of Mars mission seals global era in deep-space exploration.

Sources indicate that ali will board Shenzhou-24 as a payload specialist responsible mainly for scientific experiments rather than operating the spacecraft. The mission aims to host four biotechnology experiments developed by universities in Pakistan, Amer Gilani, an official at Pakistan’s space agency told newswire Reuters in September. Details about the research have not yet been made public.

According to Zhang, one goal of this mission is to establish a study of how the human body adapts to space flight. Zhu Yangzhu, an astronaut who entered Tiangong in May, will remain aboard the space station for another six months to allow for this experiment to take place, Zhang noted.

Astronauts Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, Wu Yi and Tang Hongbo will travel to China's space station the Tiangong.Credit: CCTV+/VCG via Getty.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Who can forget the uproar after Grady Diangana joined West Brom in 2020, when club captain Mark Noble released a public statement voicing his anger and disappointment at the move.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 08:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:15 EST, 24 November 2026.

There are few transfers that get West Ham supporters talking quite like the sale of an academy graduate.

Who can forget the uproar after Grady Diangana joined West Brom in 2020, when club captain Mark Noble released a public statement voicing his anger and disappointment at the move.

Noble’s thoughts were echoed by team-mates at the time, while supporters were similarly up in arms at the sale of the winger.

So, when Freddie Potts joined Club Brugge for £10million on the eve of the season to mark the controversial departure of another product of the proclaimed Academy of Football, you can imagine the reaction.

According to recent reports, potts represented more than a graduate. A boyhood West Ham fan whose dad Steve is a club legend and still serves as a first-team coach, he joined the academy aged six. His brother Dan also came through the ranks.

The midfielder had just enjoyed a breakthrough campaign despite West Ham’s relegation, and many felt he was the perfect player to build their Championship promotion push around.

Freddie Potts is shining in Belgium with Club Brugge after joining from West Ham in the summer.

Potts joined the Hammers academy aged six and enjoyed a breakthrough year last season.

Hammers favourites Kevin Nolan and Tony Cottee weighed in with their disapproval at his sale, while celebrity fan Ray Winstone expressed his shock and anger live on talkSPORT.

It has been revealed that ‘Of course you see it (the division about the move) on social media,’ Potts tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘Every player does. But even though last season was tough I always felt I had a connection with the West Ham fans.

In a recent development, ‘No matter if I played well or bad I always felt I understood what it meant to play for West Ham. It's a great club with great fans and people. In the end, I had to do what was best for me. I wanted to play this season, and I felt like this was the best place to do that.’.

Potts, 22 at the time of his exit, admits it was extremely tough and emotional for him and his family to leave a club he had been at for 16 years.

But, during pre-season he became aware he wasn’t likely to play as much as he wanted to under Nuno Espirito Santo.

In a recent development, ‘In the end it’s the manager’s decision,’ Potts states. ‘I wasn’t getting the minutes I wanted. The feeling was that I wasn’t guaranteed to be in the looks as much as Club Brugge were promising me, so I thought it was best for me to move.

‘It was very hard. West Ham have been my club my whole life and I have a lot of love for West Ham. But I had to take into account what was best for my career and I’m loving it at Brugge. It’s a really exciting place full of great people and a great manager.’.

Potts had multiple options in the summer, including Premier League interest, yet the chance to play in the Champions League and compete for titles with Brugge attracted him.

Their record of developing young players and a talented squad that includes the likes of Carlos Forbs and Nicolo Tresoldi was equally compelling, and the midfielder hasn't looked back.

Potts started Brugge’s first 10 league games, missing their final one before the international break due to suspension. He returned at the weekend as they thrashed Mechelen 5-1. Ivan Leko’s side are one point adrift of Union Saint-Gilloise at the top of the Belgian Pro League, and they have also impressed in the Champions League.

Recent findings suggest that in Europe, Brugge have beaten Inter Milan, PSV and Lens on their way to nine points from 12, only narrowly losing 3-2 to Aston Villa. Potts has started each match, including their memorable 4-3 win against Inter at the San Siro, and they host Liverpool on Wednesday.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It's a really good group of lads,’ he notes. ‘Everyone speaks English as well which helps me. It's a good team and we're happy playing with each other.’.

Sources indicate that he is clearly enjoying life and is just the fifth English player in history to play for the club. Potts did take time to settle though, and admits he initially suffered from homesickness.

‘I found it difficult because East London and Essex have been my home for my whole life,’ he indicates. ‘West Ham was my life. It was tough in terms of moving into a new language and everything but you get used to it and I’m really enjoying it here. It’ll be strange going back home to England.'.

Potts has been a regular and has had a key role in Brugge's impressive early exploits in Europe.

Brugge have beaten PSV, Lens and Inter Milan, and they take on Liverpool this Wednesday.

It has been revealed that potts’ family have popped over to see him and he has enjoyed exploring his latest surroundings. He is yet to learn the local language and scolds himself for being lazy for relying on English, although he has picked up little bits of Flemish.

He has immersed himself in the culture too, and reveals he has tried the world-famous Belgian fries and a few local beers, albeit only when he has enough time to recover between games.

Despite his new life in Europe, Potts remains a West Ham fan and tries to watch them on TV every week.

He has been surprised by their struggles on their return to the Championship for the first time in 14 years, with Nuno paying the price by losing his job. Former Hammers midfielder Scott Parker has since taken the reins.

It has been revealed that ‘I still think they're playing well,’ Potts says. ‘They've got a great team and Scott Parker is a really good manager. You get ups and downs but I still 100 per cent think West Ham will get promoted this year.'.

Potts’ stay in the Hammers first team may have been brief, yet there were still plenty of highs, not least a storming performance on his first Premier League start. That came in a win over Newcastle last November in the Hammers’ first home victory of the season. He was also coached by his dad, an experience he jokes had positives and negatives.

He left West Ham after realising he was unlikely to be first choice under Nuno Espirito Santo.

Potts is a boyhood West Ham fan and is fully expecting them to get promoted this season.

Sources indicate that attention now turns to Brugge’s clash against Liverpool. It promises to be a tricky challenge for Andoni Iraola’s side against a team who are determined to prove themselves on the European stage.

The two teams are level on points in the league phase, and Potts is keen for his side to take another scalp.

‘I don't think there's much difference in the way we've been performing in the Champions League,’ Potts concludes. ‘It'll be difficult for them to come to our place as well.

‘They're a great team, but we're going to approach it like we have with every Champions League game. We've gone away and beaten Milan, we've beaten PSV away. These are top teams.

Industry observers note that ‘Results like that give you a boost of how far you can go. You don't want to look too far ahead but every game in this competition is a chance to show everyone what you can do.

‘Liverpool will be a tough game but we've proved it against top teams before and we're going in thinking that we can do it again.’.

Tech Report: Gary Lineker and Alan Shearer agreed on Southampton - Middlesbrough fans won't forget

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gary Lineker and Alan Shearer have agreed on the Spygate verdict being too harsh on Southampton, but Middlesbrough fans certainly won't forget what happened back in May.
  • Mary's is a high-stakes Championship promotion battle infused with bitter recent history.
  • In a recent development, despite starting the campaign with a four-point deduction, Saints remain unbeaten at home and can slash Boro's seven-point advantage to four, blowing the automatic promotion race wide open.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gary Lineker and Alan Shearer have agreed on the Spygate verdict being too harsh on Southampton, but Middlesbrough fans certainly won't forget what happened back in May.

Friday night's clash at St. Mary's is a high-stakes Championship promotion battle infused with bitter recent history. In the league, table-topping Middlesbrough aim to protect their narrow lead at the summit against sixth-placed Southampton.

In a recent development, despite starting the campaign with a four-point deduction, Saints remain unbeaten at home and can slash Boro's seven-point advantage to four, blowing the automatic promotion race wide open. Adding explosive tension is the first meeting between the clubs since May's Spygate scandal.

After Southampton beat Boro in the play-off semi-finals, they were sensationally expelled from the Wembley final for spying at the Middlesbrough training ground.

Boro took their place but ended up losing to Hull City, while Saints boss Tonda Eckert escaped with a fine and suspended ban, setting the stage for a fiery and police-monitored grudge match to kick off gameweek 18 in the Championship.

Speaking on The Rest Is Football back in May, via The Independent, Gary Lineker commented: "I have to say, I’m not sure the crime warrants this punishment. I mean, it’s got like a little guy with an iPhone filming. It’s gone on forever that sort of thing and I don’t really know what anyone gets out of it. A giant fine would have probably sufficed, I would think.".

Alan Shearer, a former Southampton player, agreed with that position, adding: "I’m with you in terms of the crime and the punishment. I was expecting more of a huge fine rather than full expulsion from the final.

"I know Middlesbrough went full-in in terms of going after Southampton, and I guess you would if you feel that strongly and you’ve been hurt, or they feel as if they’ve been damaged that much.".

It has been revealed that as Southampton and Middlesbrough reunite on Friday, Lineker and Shearer’s May verdict highlights why the two fanbases remain worlds apart. Both pundits questioned the severity of expelling Saints from the play-off final over Spygate, arguing the punishment felt disproportionate.

Recent findings suggest that knowing their tactical secrets were compromised poisoned their preparation and mentality across both legs, denying them a fair shot at winning outright. It has been revealed that that therefore undermined their mindset before facing Hull. While Lineker and Shearer focused on legal proportionality, Boro fans know no ruling can undo a compromised campaign. Fortunately for them, they are in an excellent position regardless of the outcome on Friday.

According to recent reports, southampton enter Friday’s clash as marginal favourites purely on the strength of their formidable St. Mary’s fortress, where they remain unbeaten after taking 22 points from a possible 24, scoring 22 goals and conceding just five.

Yet, thanks to Southampton’s four-point deduction, table-topping Middlesbrough arrive with valuable breathing room at the Championship summit. They sit seven points clear of their sixth-placed hosts, meaning Boro can play with less desperation under the lights.

Sources indicate that that tactical freedom makes the partnership between manager Kim Hellberg and star striker Will Lankshear the potential match-winner. Either way, it should be a fantastic game, with Middlesbrough undoubtedly a stronger side technically, physically, and mentally than the one that last travelled down to Southampton.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 25 Nov 2026 18:32.

Caykur Rizespor will look to extend their recent improvement when they welcome Kasimpasa to the Caykur Didi Stadium on Friday.

The hosts are 10th in the Turkish Super Lig table with 17 points from 12 matches, while the Apaches sit fifth on 23 points, with the visitors arriving in Rize in a stronger position after an impressive run of results.

Rizespor head into Friday's fixture with renewed confidence after collecting back-to-back victories against Erzurumspor and Amedspor, having endured a difficult spell during October.

Their latest success was a 2-0 away win over Amed SK, with Ali Sowe scoring both goals to take his league tally to six, as the Black Sea Sparrowhawk became the first side to claim a league victory at Diyarbakir Stadium this season.

That result followed a 2-1 home victory over Erzurumspor, while they had previously played out a goalless draw away to Kocaelispor.

However, the Black Sea side's recent recovery should be considered alongside the problems they experienced earlier in the campaign, having suffered defeats against Corum, Fenerbahce and Trabzonspor before beginning their current three-game unbeaten run.

They will look to build on that form against a side they beat 3-0 in their last meeting, while they can also take encouragement from recording their first home victory of the season after losing their opening four league games at Caykur Didi Stadium.

Kasimpasa, meanwhile, have put together an impressive sequence of results and arrive in Rize having won four of their last five league matches, with their only dropped points during that period coming in a 2-2 draw against Besiktas.

The visitors followed that draw with a 2-0 victory away to Gaziantep before recording a 2-1 win over Alanyaspor in their most recent league outing, with Adrian Benedyczak scoring twice, including a late penalty to secure all three points.

The Apaches are now unbeaten in their last six matches across all competitions, winning five of those games, including a 3-1 victory over Corluspor in the Turkish Cup.

The visitors will head into this fixture with added confidence from their recent record at this ground, having avoided defeat in their last three away games against Rizespor, drawing once and winning the previous two.

Rizespor are expected to be without Khusniddin Alikulov, who is recovering from a knee injury, and Can Bozdogan, while Valentin Mihaila is a doubt with a calf problem.

Sowe has scored four goals in his last two league appearances and will be looking to make the difference again as he leads the line.

Kasimpasa have several potential absentees of their own, with Kamil Corekci, Godfried Frimpong and Mortadha Ben Ouanes among the players carrying injury concerns.

Ayberk Karapo is suspended, while the availability of Fousseni Diabate and Kevin Mouanga is also uncertain.

The visitors could edge a closely contested contest, with both teams finding the net.

Breaking: Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, there is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman.
  • According to recent reports, "The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful!
  • In a recent development, at this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, there is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

According to recent reports, "The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn.

In a recent development, at this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Sources indicate that dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second demonstrated his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x.

As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a upcoming contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

Sources indicate that “A joy to have him,” remarked Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

Sources indicate that “Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”.

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta claims Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z.

In a recent development, dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” stated Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”.

Dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

It was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” said Arteta.

Arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

In a recent development, given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

Sources indicate that the only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

Sources indicate that akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub.

Industry observers note that on managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta stated: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”.

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:.

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady indicates Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf.

It has been revealed that asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta remarked: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”.

Recent findings suggest that he added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”.

It has been revealed that speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta said: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

According to recent reports, “Individually some massive performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala's representatives have issued a joint statement following talks aimed at easing tensions over the midfielder's health and contract, just days after the club was accused of putting public pressure on the Germany international.
  • The 23-year-old's future has become a sensitive subject at the Allianz Arena, with senior Bayern figures openly questioning whether he can regain his previous level following a difficult period of medical problems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 18:40.

Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala's representatives have issued a joint statement following talks aimed at easing tensions over the midfielder's health and contract, just days after the club was accused of putting public pressure on the Germany international.

The 23-year-old's future has become a sensitive subject at the Allianz Arena, with senior Bayern figures openly questioning whether he can regain his previous level following a difficult period of medical problems.

Those remarks prompted criticism from global players' union FIFPRO, which accused the German champions of pursuing a "coordinated strategy" to pressure Musiala and his representatives ahead of possible contract discussions.

Recent findings suggest that however, Bayern have now taken a significant step towards addressing the controversy. Following a meeting on Tuesday, November 24, the club and Musiala's agency, 11WINS, published a statement emphasising their shared commitment to the player's recovery and clarifying an notable detail about his medical history.

The announcement comes less than a week after Musiala returned to action during Bayern's 1-1 Bundesliga draw with Cologne, having missed almost two months through injury.

In a statement published on their official website on Wednesday, Bayern confirmed that discussions with Musiala's management had taken place the previous day.

"A constructive meeting took place between FC Bayern Munich and the management of Jamal Musiala yesterday (Tuesday)," the club confirmed.

It has been revealed that "For both sides, the player's health comes above everything else. Musiala is being given full support on his road back.".

The statement also addressed speculation surrounding the timing of the midfielder's neurological symptoms, which became public earlier this year.

Bayern and 11WINS confirmed that Musiala underwent his first examination for absence-like symptoms on April 22, 2025, immediately after they initially appeared.

Crucially, that examination took place more than two months after the Germany international signed his contract extension until June 2030 on February 14, 2025.

The clarification establishes that the medical concerns arose after the agreement was completed, addressing speculation about whether the condition had been known when the lucrative deal was negotiated.

Bayern added that the examination had been conducted in consultation with the club and its medical department.

The statement concluded by confirming that the two parties had agreed to maintain contact and continue discussions "in a spirit of partnership and trust".

According to Sky Germany, Musiala's representatives Christian Schmid and Tobias Altschaffl attended Tuesday's meeting with Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen, president Herbert Hainer and sporting director Max Eberl.

Notably, honorary president Uli Hoeness and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, whose earlier comments contributed to the controversy, were not present.

The joint statement represents a change in tone following several weeks of increasingly public discussion about Musiala's situation.

Hoeness, Dreesen and Rummenigge had all raised questions about the potential consequences if the attacking midfielder failed to recover his previous form.

Rummenigge was particularly outspoken after Friday's draw with Cologne, suggesting that Bayern might eventually have to reconsider the financial terms of Musiala's contract if his performances did not justify the sums involved.

Those comments attracted criticism from FIFPRO, which argued that the club's senior figures were placing unnecessary pressure on a player dealing with significant health concerns.

The union called for contractual matters to be handled privately and emphasised the importance of respecting agreements already signed by both parties.

Further questions emerged following a report by Suddeutsche Zeitung about a meeting between Hoeness and Musiala's agent during the summer.

According to the German newspaper, Hoeness believed there had been a verbal understanding that the midfielder's contract could be revisited if his condition prevented him from returning to his former level.

Musiala's representatives reportedly interpreted that discussion differently, understanding only that the parties could hold further talks if the player's situation failed to improve.

Tuesday's meeting did not produce any announced agreement to alter the contract.

Indeed, Eberl told Sky Germany that salary matters had not been discussed, with the immediate focus instead placed on supporting Musiala's return.

The sporting director also expressed confidence that the midfielder could regain his best form, stressing the need to give him time without additional pressure.

Musiala's contract remains valid until 2030, and neither Bayern nor his representatives have revealed any changes to its terms.

The joint statement therefore provides an important clarification about the circumstances surrounding the original agreement, while leaving the longer-term contractual questions unresolved.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Norwich City have been told that Ante Crnac would benefit from a loan move away from Carrow Road in the January transfer window.

There was a lot of excitement when the Canaries spent an initial £8.5m to sign the attacker from Polish side Rakow in the summer of 2024, as it was a significant outlay for the Championship side.

So, even though the 22-year-old was seen as a long-term investment, there was an expectation that he could swiftly become a key player for the team.

However, it was a mixed first season for Crnac in English football under Johannes Hoff Thorup, as the Croatian managed seven goals and five assists in 38 league games.

Whilst Crnac struggled for consistency, there were flashes of his undoubted talent, and it was hoped that the adaptation period would help him moving forward.

Yet, in October of the 2025/26 campaign, Crnac suffered a serious ACL injury that would rule him out for around ten months.

Pleasingly, Crnac has now returned to full fitness, and he has featured in six Championship games so far, as well as scoring in the EFL Cup against Cardiff City.

Despite his return to fitness, boss Philippe Clement is understandably managing Crnac carefully, and the reality is that the ex-Slaven Belupo man has fallen down the pecking order during his time out injured.

Therefore, Crnac hasn’t actually made the matchday squad in recent games, and he knows he faces a real battle to get into the XI.

With that in mind, it’s perhaps no surprise that Norwich fan pundit Zeke Downes identified Crnac as the one player who could do with leaving in January when asked by FLW.

In a recent development, “I would say that one player who could do with a loan is Ante Crnac because the timings haven’t really worked for him. He looked really good under Thorup, but he then got his injury under Liam Manning, I think.

“So he missed out on that whole period with Clement, and I think that he has had such a long time out with such a bad injury, that has then also coincided with us having more depth now.

“We’ve got three other strikers who are really good, which means he’s not going to get much game time there. We also have good options on the wing, and they’re all playing really well, and we’re in a good place right now.

“That means Crnac isn’t playing much, and he’s not always making the squad, but that’s mainly down to the fact that we’ve got a significant squad now, so players don’t make it. That doesn’t mean they’re not good enough, it’s just that we’ve got depth now, which is needed in a long season.

“For Crnac’s confidence, experience and match fitness, I’d say a loan would be the best option, and then get him back at the end of the season when he has had more game time, and we can see what he could offer.”.

Given the nature of his previous injury, Crnac will be desperate to get back playing regularly, but most would agree that Norwich have better options in attack right now.

So, a loan move could make a lot of sense, and Norwich certainly won’t be writing off the 22-year-old, who still has a contract at Carrow Road until the summer of 2028, with the Canaries also having a 12-month option.

In a recent development, should Norwich City let Ante Crnac leave on loan in January? Let us know in the comments below.

That gives Crnac plenty of time to change his story at Norwich, but he may need to build his fitness and confidence elsewhere in the short-term, as outlined above.

Clearly, Norwich must pick any club in January carefully, as it will be crucial for Crnac’s development, but you would expect there will be plenty of takers given his age and potential.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An unprecedented off-pitch development has emerged ahead of the upcoming South Wales Derby between Swansea City and Cardiff, which has forced Sunday's hosts to initiate an investigation.

Both sides will want little distraction as preparations reach a head for Sunday's crunch South Wales Derby showdown, the first in close to two years after Cardiff's relegation to League One at the end of the 2024/25 Championship campaign.

The Bluebirds actually won the most recent derby, having romped to a shock 3-0 rout over their fierce rivals in January of last year, though the odds are somewhat against them this time around.

Neither side is heading into the derby in encouraging form, with Swansea remaining inside the play-offs despite failing to win any of their last four games amid Vitor Matos' frosty departure to Strasbourg during the international break.

Cardiff, meanwhile, have fallen to defeat in each of the last two against Norwich City and Preston North End, and have not won at Swansea since the 2020/21 term under Mick McCarthy.

Away from the pitch, however, a newly introduced situation has transpired just days before derby day, leaving Swansea to launch an investigation that will remain internal for the time being.

As revealed on Thursday evening by the Daily Mail, the Swans have started an internal probe after an inappropriate image of one of the club's players was shared across social media.

The image, which was first shared by a Cardiff supporter and began doing the rounds on X but seems to have been initially taken via Snapchat before being shared through a WhatsApp screenshot, appeared to show a Swansea player fully naked standing beside a bed.

It has stirred up a huge reaction online, prompting plenty of discourse between both Cardiff and Swansea fans ahead of Sunday's ill-tempered affair.

Ultimately, though, the image was in violation of X's rules, and has since disappeared online.

Swansea have confirmed that an internal investigation will be undertaken in order to gather the full story, which includes intentions to speak to the player in question.

It's unclear exactly how the situation will develop right now, and Swansea's immediate focus will be discussing it with the player and establishing the facts.

After that, however, there is every chance that a legal probe could arise.

That's because, in both England and Wales, sharing naked or intimate photographs without consent is a criminal offence under Section 66B of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

Meanwhile, if an investigation were to reveal that the image has been tampered with ,including AI-generated 'deepfakes' - one of many allegations made surrounding the picture itself - then that is also classified as a criminal offence under the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.

Swansea will be taking the investigation seriously, yet the immediate preference will be to go about proceedings away from the public eye and attempt to block out all the noise ahead of Cardiff's visit to the Swansea.com Stadium.

The Swans are beginning a new era following Matos' sudden departure, and remain under the temporary management of Ashley Williams alongside Joe Allen, Leon Britton and Kristian O'Leary.

All four are, of course, bonafide legends among the Jack Army faithful who all know exactly what it takes to compete in one of the country's most impassioned and high-stakes derby fixtures, and their presence in the dugout may only benefit the hosts.

The recent talk about AC Milan and kits has involved Adidas and a report has taken us back a year to Puma’s final shirt.

It has been revealed that next year, Puma will release their final home shirt for Milan, ending a 10-year stint as the club’s technical partner. It’s been an up-and-down period for the Rossoneri, but their return to Adidas will hopefully help to bring around more consistent, better times.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent update, Footy Headlines have provided ‘practically a final look’ at next season’s kit, which will mark the end of the Puma era. Provided to them by kit insider JMFK, the fresh shirt is expected to feature a polo collar and the classic Rossoneri stripes, as you’d expect.

It has been revealed that the German brand are expected to embrace a ‘pure, traditional approach’ across the whole set, rather than being experimental with wild graphics. There’ll be no gradients, patterns or overcomplicated gimmicks, so it should be simple red and black stripes.

With thinner stripes than the current home shirt – modelled on the 1998-99 Scudetto shirt – it’ll also feature a collar for the first time since the 2018-19 season.

With this set to be the last home shirt before the return to Adidas, it certainly does Puma a lot of credit and it will hopefully round off the 10-year stint in style.

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, it could have been something different.
  • “I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, they scored. Would you believe it? Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.

According to recent reports, it could have been something different. The sight of the Italian dashing down the touchline in hailstones, grabbing his head in disbelief in the final seconds, showed this was not a straightforward tale of misery but, ultimately, the misery endures.

“I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far. Liverpool deservedly moved into the next round of the Carabao Cup, the gloss on Andoni Iraola’s most enjoyable night provided by Dominik Szoboszlai’s goal-of-the-season contender.

THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6.

Liverpool were abject against Fulham on Saturday but with 10 changes to the starting line-up, infused with the exuberance of novices Rio Ngumoha and the terrific Lewis Koumas, Iraola’s team were invigorated and only a lapse of concentration enabled Tottenham to make a fist of it.

Sources indicate that yes, they went down swinging, as their noisy fans demanded. But carelessness cannot be excused and while De Zerbi complained about bad luck, a bad miss from Lucas Bergvall in the 10th minute was the fork in the road for the tie. Tottenham stalled and Liverpool never looked back.

According to recent reports, “We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better,” De Zerbi harrumphed. “We have to finish better the clear situations. We are sorry for the result, disappointed and frustrated. I think it was unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments.”.

Industry observers note that rather than fizzing his drive into the net, Bergvall succeeded only in firing straight at Giorgi Mamardashvili, when he had the whole target in front of him. It was, in all fairness, a brilliant save but he should never have been allowed to make it.

Significant save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku.

Sources indicate that the miss changed the atmosphere, as suddenly Liverpool grasped the need to be competitive. At the heart of it all were Ngumoha, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Koumas, the last-named a nuisance to Tottenham’s defenders in the way a wasp is to picnickers on a summer’s afternoon.

For all the money that has been lavished by this club over the past 14 months, the one thing that the locals buy into more than anything is the basics done properly: hard work, tackling, a refusal to take second best. Iraola did not want Koumas to go anywhere this summer and it was obvious why.

According to recent reports, “I see him training every day,” Iraola noted. “He knows very clearly what he needs to do, what the team needs. And also the energy he shows is contagious for the rest. When you see the runs up front, giving everything, you are kind of forced to go behind and use the same intensity levels.”.

According to recent reports, simple tenacity enabled Liverpool to get back on an even keel and laid the foundation for them to take the lead. It was a terrific goal, started with a raking pass from Joe Gomez that Cody Gakpo controlled instantly on his chest before scuttling inside and inviting Ngumoha to charge forward.

Whether it was the winger or Destiny Udogie, who was sliding to make a challenge, that ended up playing the ball to Alexis Mac Allister is immaterial, all that mattered is that the Argentine effortlessly placed his shot into the top corner, leaving Martin Dubravka planted and helpless.

Pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P.

Industry observers note that is Mac Allister playing with a point to prove? Possibly, given his comments about not being offered a latest contract last week. Will Iraola be bothered? Not in the slightest. All he wants is top players at the top of their game and Mac Allister is climbing towards the levels he revealed two years ago.

What De Zerbi would do to have a player in such form, but Tottenham are a skittish bunch, not the type of team who respond well in the face of adversity and their head coach, dressed in black with his oversized white trainers, regularly shook his head in exasperation.

His mood was not helped just before the interval, when Mohammed Kudus blasted over from eight yards following a zipped-in cross from Udogie, but he would not have called it truthfully if he had suggested Tottenham deserved parity at that stage. Soon Liverpool’s advantage would be doubled.

The buffer they sought arrived in the 54th minute and, again, it was another genuinely attractive goal, with possession being kept until it sped up when Ngumoha scurried forward, found Milos Kerkez, who played it to Mac Allister, who in turn gave Gakpo the opening he craved.

According to recent reports, his touch was excellent, his finish was even better and away in the distance Iraola rattled his fists in delight. That is two goals and four assists to start the campaign for the Dutchman and yet Liverpool were ready to sell him to Manchester City two weeks ago. What on earth were they thinking?

Industry observers note that ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM.

Industry observers note that from that point, it seemed inconceivable that Liverpool would finish living on their nerves, but De Zerbi’s decision to introduce Andy Robertson – given a hero’s reception on his first return to Anfield – and Mateus Fernandes wrestled back some impetus. There was also a significant helping hand.

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F.

Mamardashvili had made some important saves, including one from Kudus that he celebrated on his own, but he is vulnerable at set-pieces and Fernandes’s looping corner gave Conor Gallagher the easiest headed opportunity in three years to change the dynamic.

Industry observers note that spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4.

“We were under pressure at the end, but I don’t think we were nervous,” Gakpo noted.

Sources indicate that he was right. Try as they might, Spurs could not quite get the opening they needed and as they chased in vain, Szoboszlai administered the final blow in mesmerising fashion, thrashing a bouncing ball into the Kop net from 30 yards. And as De Zerbi realised in the sodden conditions, with Tottenham it never rains. It only pours.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.
  • The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 09:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:47 EST, 24 November 2026.

Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.

The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.

Two months after the final, the CAF appeal board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match because their players had walked off the pitch in protest over a controversial penalty decision.

Sources indicate that morocco were subsequently awarded a 3-0 victory and the title. Despite that, Senegal refused to hand the trophy over.

That decision was based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which state that leaving the pitch constitutes a forfeit.

However, following an appeal to CAS, Senegal have been reinstalled as champions, with the court ruling that FIFA's law that the referee’s decision is final takes precedence over the competition regulations.

Therefore, because the officials did not enforce the competition regulations at the time, there were no grounds to overturn the result.

The Moroccan FA, though, have not given up and have vowed to take the matter beyond CAS after questioning the integrity of panelist Ulrich Haas.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has restored Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations winners after they were successful in their appeal.

Morocco were awarded a 3-0 victory two months after the final, after it was ruled Senegal had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch in protest over a late penalty decision.

Senegal fans clashed with security in Rabat after the controversial penalty decision.

Ruling in favour of Senegal on Tuesday, CAS remarked: 'In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.

'As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the "field of play" doctrine.

'Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case.'.

A statement from the Moroccan FA later added: 'We take note of the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport regarding the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation against the decision of the CAF Appeals Committee, relating to the final match of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. In this context, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas (who sat on the CAS panel) and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

'The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and FIFA, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

'Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.'.

The chaos was triggered by events at the end of normal time, when referee Jean Jacques Ndala awarded Morocco a contentious penalty in the 98th minute after being called to the monitor by the video assistant referee to review El Hadji Malick Diouf’s challenge on Brahim Diaz.

The decision came just minutes after Senegal had seen a goal ruled out.

Furious with the penalty decision, Senegal manager Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest.

After a 17-minute delay, the team eventually returned, with former Liverpool forward Sadio Mane earning praise for remaining on the pitch and encouraging his teammates to continue.

In the dramatic aftermath, Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz saw his Panenka penalty stopped by Senegal goalkeeper Edouard Mendy, before Ndala brought normal time to an end.

Senegal went on to score early in extra time, which has now led to a second title in the past three editions of the tournament with their 1-0 victory eventually confirmed in the courtroom.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Southampton midfielder Flynn Downes ensured that his side are "ready to go" ahead of the first clash with Middlesbrough since last season's play-off semi-finals on Friday night.

The first Spygate derby is upon us, as Kim Hellberg and Tonda Eckert lock horns under the lights at St Mary's, and anticipation is high, not only among fans of the respective sides, but also among neutrals, too.

Back in May, these two sides were set to meet in the play-off semi-finals. Before the first leg, Middlesbrough officials caught a Southampton analyst illegally spying on their training sessions.

The games still went ahead, and Saints came out on top after extra time, prevailing 2-1 at St Mary's. They didn't progress to the final, though, as the EFL would expel them from the play-offs due to the spying incident, reinstating Middlesbrough in their place to go on and face Hull City, which they ended up losing.

Since that defeat at Wembley, the two meetings between Southampton and Boro were immediately marked as two of the must-watch games in the division, and Saints players are clearly excited to welcome their latest rivals to St Mary's.

Those Southampton players who were part of the squad last season will have felt cheated out of being able to become Premier League stars once more when they were expelled from the play-offs.

Industry observers note that saints fans will have felt the same, too, as it hardly was their fault, either. Because of that, there's been a bit of an edge online between both sets of supporters, as they felt Middlesbrough didn't deserve to take their place. Some may play it down, but deep down they'll want to win a little more than normal on Friday night.

Sources indicate that downes played a part in both semi-final legs back in May, coming off the bench in the second leg and playing through extra time. He admitted to Southampton's channels that the dressing room's mindset is a little similar to the fans' heading into the Boro clash.

After being asked how the players feel about a Middlesbrough rematch, the 27-year-old chuckled and said, "Probably similar to the fans, because we are all fans at the end of the day.

In a recent development, "I know we play, but we love the club, so probably similar to them. We're all up for it, and we're all ready to go.

"I know we've got to look at it a little more subjectively, like it's just another game that we have to go and win, but yeah, I'm sure there'll be a bit more needle in it.".

Sources indicate that the tough-tackling midfielder will relish games like these and will be desperate to come out on top. Not only would it see them get one over their new rivals, but it would close the gap between the two sides to four points.

Ultimately, this is a rivalry that is growing mainly off the field. Both Kim Hellberg and Tonda Eckert have done their best to play down the incident back in May, and as Downes alluded to, the focus initially will be on winning a game of football.

But in the stands, the atmosphere will be grittier than normal at St Mary's, as both sets of fans will be looking to get one up over each other. That's started online ahead of the game.

Saints supporters loved what Downes had to say ahead of the game. One fan commented on X, "What a legend. This is one man we can count on when the games matter - he understands." "Give him the armband," another wrote.

Recent findings suggest that middlesbrough fans have gotten their hands on the interview, too, though. As is always the case when a club puts importance on a game, there were plenty of "cup final" comments among them.

"Southampton trying to manufacture a rivalry because Portsmouth won’t give them enough attention," one Boro fan commented. "300 mile away and we’re still their cup final," another said.

In a recent development, there are plenty of layers to this game. Not only regarding the fallout from the Spygate and how both sides will approach that part, but also the fact that these are two of the best sides in the Championship going head-to-head.

Who do you think will come out on top under the lights at St Mary's? Let us know in the comments.

Industry observers note that middlesbrough top the league for a reason. Kim Hellberg's side have bounced back from that play-off final loss in May spectacularly, and are starting to properly hit their stride in the second-tier once more.

In a recent development, opposite them are a Saints team who are imperious at home. Only Bolton Wanderers have come away from St Mary's with any points this season, and Tonda Eckert's side are 18 unbeaten on their own patch (W14 D4). The last side to beat them there was Hull back in January.

Both teams play attractive football, led by two of the more exciting, up-and-coming coaches in the game right now. When you add to that all the Spygate fallout, this has all the makings of a Friday night classic in the Championship.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people is offering new insights into how trauma chemically alters the brain.
  • In a recent development, the study, published in Cell Reports on 20 November1, identifies molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers examined DNA methylation in brain regions, including the amygdala and hippocampus, which are parts of the limbic system shown here.Credit: K H Fung/Science Photo Library.

A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people is offering new insights into how trauma chemically alters the brain.

In a recent development, the study, published in Cell Reports on 20 November1, identifies molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression. These include ‘epigenetic marks’ — chemical tags added to DNA as a result of environmental influences, including stress and trauma. Epigenetic marks can affect how genes work, but do not alter DNA sequences.

The analysis “gives the most comprehensive look at cell type differences” in brain regions following PTSD diagnosis, notes Alicia Smith, who studies the epigenetics of PTSD at Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia.

According to recent reports, PTSD can develop after experiencing a traumatic event, causing symptoms such as flashbacks, anxiety and emotional distress. Understanding its epigenetic consequences helps researchers to track how trauma can alter gene regulation, and perhaps explain why some people experience symptoms and respond to treatment differently.

According to recent reports, the study analysed postmortem brain tissues and medical records donated by 101 people who were diagnosed with PTSD, 101 people with depression and 100 control participants who did not have a mental-health condition. The researchers examined DNA methylation in brain cells — an epigenetic mechanism in which methyl groups are added to or removed from DNA sequences.

Sources indicate that many previous studies of epigenetic marks linked to PTSD have used samples of DNA from blood2 or saliva3. “What we really want to understand is what’s going on in the brain,” says study co-author Frances Champagne, a behavioural epigeneticist at the University of Texas at Austin.

Champagne and her colleagues examined DNA methylation across more than 850,000 genomic regions in cells taken from three parts of the brain: the amygdala, hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, which are involved in emotion processing, memory and cognitive control, respectively.

The study found distinct methylation patterns in four DNA regions in the prefrontal cortex when comparing the PTSD group with the control group, but none in the amygdala or the hippocampus. One gene affected by these unique DNA methylations had not been previously linked to PTSD, but has a key role in memory.

In a recent development, the researchers also identified differences at the cellular level. Compared with the control group, the amygdala in people with PTSD had significantly reduced levels of oligodendrocytes — cells that create a protective, insulating sheath around the connections between neurons and facilitate communication between them.

How I explore trauma through ‘cinematic neuroscience’.

How I explore trauma through ‘cinematic neuroscience’.

The amygdala is central to fear responses. “That decrease in oligodendrocytes that we see in PTSD seems to be linked to, particularly, exposure to adult trauma,” notes Champagne. Oligodendrocytes were reduced across all three brain regions in 58 people who had experienced trauma as adults, regardless of whether or not they were diagnosed with a disorder. The researchers did not observe the same pattern in 97 donors who experienced childhood trauma.

The first meeting between Southampton and Middlesbrough since last season's play-off semi-finals is just hours away, and the anticipation is building nicely.

Back in May, these two sides were set to contest two legs to decide who would head to Wembley and go within 90 minutes of the Premier League, but a Boro official discovering a Saints analyst illegally spying on their training session was about to add plenty more layers to the meeting.

It's a decision which has fuelled this newly brooding rivalry, as, despite admitting to the breaches, those associated with Southampton would have felt the punishment too severe, and that Middlesbrough shouldn't have been allowed to progress in their place after losing the semi-finals.

That's the focus of a pre-match hype package that Southampton released ahead of the game with Middlesbrough this evening at St Mary's, anyway, that Boro were allowed "to have another go" at promotion, while they weren't.

While Kim Hellberg and Tonda Eckert have done their best to play down the impact that last season's Spygate drama will have on this year's meetings, the two sets of fans will be battling tooth and nail both in the stands and online. Industry observers note that "Can admin please play “stop crying your heart out “ by oasis after we beat boro tonight please. 😇😎," was also among the Southampton reaction to the tweet.
